items.title: Ziniaré : les femmes de Pousgziga aménagent leur voie d’accès grâce à une tontine
items.description: Ziniaré : les femmes de Pousgziga aménagent leur voie d'accès grâce à une tontine Ziniaré, 10 août 2026 (AIB) – Les habitantes du quartier Pousgziga, au secteur 2 de Ziniaré, ont lancé une initiative communautaire pour améliorer l'état de la voie d'accès à leurs habitations. Réunies au sein d'un regroupement de femmes, elles ont mobilisé des ressources à travers une tontine afin de financer les premiers travaux de réhabilitation. Confrontées depuis plusieurs années au mauvais état de cette voie, les femmes de Pousgziga ont décidé de passer à l'action. À l'aide des fonds collectés grâce à leur tontine, elles ont acquis de la terre pour reboucher les grands trous qui rendaient la circulation difficile, surtout en saison des pluies. « C'est la misère lorsque nous voulons quitter le quartier pour rejoindre le centre-ville. Cette inaccessibilité nous cause beaucoup de difficultés, notamment en cas d'évacuation sanitaire. C'est pourquoi nous, les femmes, avons décidé d'initier cette activité », a expliqué Germaine Nonguierma, membre du regroupement à l'origine de l'initiative. Pour financer les travaux, les initiatrices ont invité les habitantes à contribuer à hauteur de 5 000 FCFA par ménage. Si cette première mobilisation a permis de lancer les travaux, elles souhaitent désormais une plus grande implication de l'ensemble des résidents notamment les hommes. « Cette initiative doit être celle de tous les habitants. Nous avons commencé, mais nous appelons tous les résidents à nous rejoindre afin que nous puissions améliorer durablement cette voie », a plaidé Hadja Aïda Koné, également membre du regroupement. Sous un soleil de plomb, les tricycles acheminaient la terre pendant que les femmes, pelles à la main, rebouchaient les nids-de-poule dans une ambiance de solidarité et de détermination. Leur engagement a suscité l'admiration de plusieurs habitants du quartier. Présent sur les lieux, El Hadj Boureima Ouiya, un des sages du quartier a salué cette mobilisation citoyenne. Il a félicité les femmes pour leur sens de l'intérêt général avant d'inviter les autorités compétentes à accompagner cette initiative afin de permettre un aménagement durable de la voie. À travers cette action, les femmes de Pousgziga démontrent qu'en attendant des solutions structurelles, la solidarité communautaire peut contribuer à améliorer les conditions de vie des populations. Agence d'information du Burkina LC/ata

items.title: Eclipse solar en España, en directo | El eclipse total finaliza en el Mediterráneo
items.description: El eclipse solar total ha terminado ya. La sombra pura de la luna (umbra) ha recorrido, durante apenas unos minutos, la mitad norte de la península, desde Galicia hasta Baleares, donde ha terminado en Formentera, antes de morir sobre el Mediterráneo. Iniciado sobre Alaska, ha pasado a ser total sobre el extremo norte ruso y ha recorrido Groenlandia, el oeste de Islandia y España. Miles de personas se han desplazado a zonas donde poder ver el eclipse total, en medio de un enorme esfuerzo de las autoridades para evitar incendios y otras desgracias en un día de altísimas temperaturas. Pese a ello, varias personas han resultado heridas en un incendio que ha dañado 34 vehículos en un punto de observación en Peñíscola y se están produciendo atascos en varios puntos, principalmente en Madrid. items.title: Djerba : L’Atutax et ses partenaires agissent contre les engins de pêche fantômes
items.description: Dans le cadre du projet ECO-GEAR, l'Association tunisienne de Taxonomie (Atutax) a mené à Djerba une première mission pour repérer et retirer les engins de pêche abandonnés. Réalisée en étroite collaboration avec plusieurs acteurs de la société civile et experts locaux, cette opération a permis d'extraire des fonds marins des filets, des cordes, des hameçons ainsi que plusieurs nasses utilisées pour la pêche au crabe bleu. Cette première mission marque le coup d'envoi d'un programme d'action collective visant non seulement à retirer et valoriser ces engins abandonnés en mer, mais aussi à sensibiliser les communautés de pêcheurs à la prévention. « E t ces engins continuaient encore à pêcher… deux petits poissons, un jeune mérou brun et une badèche, étaient piégés dans les nasses. Heureusement, ils étaient encore vivants et ont pu être libérés et relâchés dans leur milieu naturel . Un rappel concret que les engins fantômes peuvent continuer à capturer des espèces non ciblées, longtemps après leur abandon », déplore l'Atutax L'Association tunisienne de Taxonomie précise que la réussite de cette intervention repose sur une collaboration avec ses partenaires : Abysse Plongée, partenaire technique, qui a assuré la sécurité et la logistique des opérations de plongée sous-marine, l'Association TunSea pour la Science Participative, nouveau partenaire du projet ECO-GEAR, a apporté son expertise terrain et Le Blue Dolphin Diving Club à Djerba, qui a accompagné et soutenu la logistique locale de la mission. Y. N. L’article Djerba : L'Atutax et ses partenaires agissent contre les engins de pêche fantômes est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Kombissiri/Retrouvailles de la 24ᵉ promotion de l’ENEP de Loumbila : un rendez-vous de renforcement de la cohésion, de la fraternité et de partage d’expériences
items.description: Burkina-Bazèga-Éducation-Retrouvailles Kombissiri/Retrouvailles de la 24ᵉ promotion de l'ENEP de Loumbila : un rendez-vous de renforcement de la cohésion, de la fraternité et de partage d'expériences Kombissiri, 10 août 2026 (AIB)-Les retrouvailles des enseignants de la 24ᵉ promotion de l'ENEP de Loumbila (2008-2009) ont eu lieu le samedi 8 août 2026 à Kombissiri. Un rendez-vous de fraternité, de solidarité et de renforcement de la cohésion, avec en ligne de mire l'organisation du 20ᵉ anniversaire de la promotion en 2029. Les enseignants de la 24ᵉ promotion de l'ENEP (École nationale des enseignants du primaire) de Loumbila 2008-2009 se sont réunis le samedi 8 août 2026 dans la cité de Kombissiri pour leurs retrouvailles. Ce rendez-vous annuel, qui constitue la 17ᵉ édition des retrouvailles de la promotion, a rassemblé plus de 80 membres venus de plusieurs régions du Burkina Faso. Pour le camarade Assimi Paré, délégué aux activités socioculturelles, représentant le délégué général de la promotion, « nos retrouvailles ne constituent pas seulement un rendez-vous de convivialité, elles sont avant tout un cadre privilégié de fraternité, de solidarité, de partage d'expériences et de renforcement de notre cohésion ». Selon le camarade Paré, les échanges au cours des travaux ont été l'occasion de faire des propositions et de recueillir les suggestions pour les préparatifs de la mise en place du comité d'organisation de la célébration du 20ᵉ anniversaire de la promotion en 2029. « À cet effet, une rencontre est prévue en 2027 à Ouagadougou afin de faciliter la mise en place officielle de ce comité représentatif et dynamique, qui aura pour mission de concevoir, coordonner et conduire les préparatifs de l'anniversaire dans un esprit de transparence et d'inclusion », a indiqué le délégué aux activités socioculturelles de la promotion. À l'ouverture des travaux des retrouvailles de la promotion, le directeur provincial de l'Éducation préscolaire, primaire et non formelle du Bazèga, le camarade Claude Ouédraogo, a félicité les enseignants de la promotion pour l'initiative des retrouvailles organisées chaque année. Il les a encouragés à maintenir cette dynamique, qui, selon lui, permet de renforcer la cohésion, la solidarité, la fraternité et le partage d'expériences, nécessaires pour la suite de leurs carrières professionnelles. Pour le camarade Paré, la mobilisation de la promotion à Kombissiri est la preuve éloquente que les liens tissés sur les bancs de l'ENEP demeurent solides et continuent de les unir, malgré les responsabilités professionnelles, familiales et les distances qui les séparent. Le rendez-vous de Kombissiri a été un cadre de convivialité et de détente pour la promotion, qui a terminé la journée dans une belle ambiance. Agence d'information du Burkina TPT/ata

items.title: Sedina Tamakloe’s release was the ‘logical conclusion’ after acquittal — Amaliba
items.description: Former Director of Legal Affairs of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC), Abraham Amaliba, says the release of former MASLOC Chief Executive Officer Sedina Tamakloe-Attionu was the “logical conclusion” following her acquittal and discharge by the Court of Appeal. According to Mr Amaliba, there was little surprise about Ms Tamakloe-Attionu’s release because the appellate court’s decision effectively cleared the way for her to regain her freedom. Speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story on Wednesday, August 12, Mr Amaliba said the normal legal process following an acquittal and discharge meant Ms Tamakloe-Attionu could walk free once the relevant period had elapsed. “That is the logical conclusion once the court said she was acquitted and discharged. Normally, there is a seven-day statutory stay of execution. After seven days, she can go home and walk free. So I didn’t expect anything apart from that.” His comments come after the Attorney-General withdrew an application seeking to stay the execution of the Court of Appeal’s judgment, paving the way for Ms Tamakloe-Attionu’s release from custody. Mr Amaliba said the Attorney-General’s decision to withdraw the application could have been informed by a review of the appellate court’s judgment. He explained that the initial decision to seek a stay was taken at a time when the Attorney-General’s Office had not yet fully reviewed the judgment. “I can only hazard a guess,” he said, suggesting that after examining the judgment, the Attorney-General may have concluded that there were insufficient grounds to pursue the matter further. Mr Amaliba also defended the government against claims by the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) that the release vindicated its earlier accusations of political interference. He argued that once an independent court had acquitted and discharged Ms Tamakloe-Attionu, the government could not simply prevent her release. “If the Supreme Court that he says he respects hadn’t acquitted and discharged the lady, even if we as a party wanted to do it, how could we have done it?” he asked. He maintained that the Court of Appeal’s decision must be respected as an independent judicial determination and should not be interpreted as evidence that the government had deliberately sought to keep Ms Tamakloe-Attionu in prison.

items.title: KUMACA launches 70th anniversary celebration with focus on shaping character and cultivating minds
items.description: Kumasi Academy (KUMACA) has begun preparations to mark seven decades of academic excellence, discipline and service to Ghana, with the launch of its 70th Anniversary Celebration on Saturday, 8 August 2026. Under the theme, “Shaping Character, Cultivating Minds and Nursing Souls,” the anniversary seeks not only to celebrate the school’s remarkable journey but also to renew its commitment to producing responsible citizens for Ghana’s future. The launch assembled alumni and students of KUMACA and the wider community, including government officials, traditional leaders, parents, and other stakeholders. The occasion provided an opportunity to reflect on the institution’s achievements while looking ahead to the challenges and opportunities of the next generation. Addressing the gathering, the Ashanti Regional Minister, Dr. Frank Amoakohene, underscored the critical role of discipline in education and personal development. He encouraged students to respect authority, honour their teachers and shun violence, stressing that discipline remains an essential bridge between aspirations and achievement. “Students gathered here, I am urging you: do not assault your teachers, do not vandalize school property even if you are in disagreement. Mob justice is one that our laws frown against. You are encouraged to use the laid-down procedures in seeking justice and seeking redress as far as any issues are concerned,” he said. The Asokore Mampong Municipal Chief Executive, Ben Abdallah Alhasan, pledged the Assembly’s support towards KUMACA’s ambition of attaining Grade A status. He assured the school community that the Assembly would work with management, the alumni, traditional authorities and parents to address the institution’s pressing needs and strengthen its development. “Education is a fundamental driver of development and its advancement must not be left to government alone,” he said. He therefore called for a collective effort to improve schools and create an environment in which students can excel and talents can be nurtured for the benefit of society. The Global President of the Kumasi Academy Past Students Association, KAPSA AKUNINI, H.E. Okunini Harry Boakye, also reaffirmed the commitment of past students to the continued development of their alma mater. He highlighted the important role alumni play in supporting teaching and learning as well as infrastructure development, while calling on past students to unite behind the school and help sustain its legacy. The emotional connection between KUMACA and its old students was perhaps best captured by Nana Boakye Yam Ababio, Nkwantakesehene and Chairperson for the occasion. “I breathe KUMACA. I feel KUMACA. I smell KUMACA. I sleep with KUMACA in my heart,” he noted. The declaration resonated strongly with the gathering, reflecting the deep bond that generations of students and alumni have developed with the school. As KUMACA looks towards its anniversary in 2027, the celebration is being positioned as more than a commemoration of the past. It is also a call to stakeholders to invest in the institution’s next chapter. The school is calling on alumni to contribute resources, mentorship and expertise; parents and guardians to partner with the school in nurturing disciplined and excellent students; and students to uphold the values of character, scholarship and service. Teachers, staff, community leaders and other stakeholders are similarly being encouraged to support initiatives aimed at improving infrastructure, student welfare and educational programmes. With a renewed emphasis on discipline, collaboration, character development and academic excellence, KUMACA is seeking to strengthen its position among Ghana’s leading schools. The anniversary therefore provides an opportunity to celebrate the past while laying the foundation for a stronger future.

items.title: Konovalets réinhumé : Zakharova accuse Kiev de perpétuer l'héritage nazi et terroriste de l’OUN
items.description: Le regime de Kiev a herite de l'ideologie et des methodes terroristes de l'Organisation des nationalistes ukrainiens (OUN), qui avait collabore avec le Troisieme Reich pendant la Seconde Guerre mondiale, a declare le 12 août Maria Zakharova, porte-parole du ministere russe des Affaires etrangeres, commentant l'exhumation a Rotterdam de la depouille du fondateur de l'OUN, Evgueni Konovalets, et sa reinhumation prevue en Ukraine qui a ete annonce e la veille par le bureau de Volodymyr Zelensky. Dans son commentaire, elle a cite des faits attestant de la collaboration de Konovalets avec l'Allemagne nazie et de son implication dans des activites terroristes. « Pour quels "merites" sanglants a-t-il ete aussi honore ? », s'est interrogee Zakharova sur sa chaîne Telegram, rappelant que Konovalets avait fait ses « debuts au combat » a Kiev en janvier 1918, lorsque des centaines d'ouvriers de l'usine Arsenal avaient ete victimes des nationalistes. « Dans un rapport de 1923, il reconnaissait lui-meme : "l'Organisation militaire ukrainienne (UVO) est entierement sous l'influence des services de renseignement allemands et fournit son appareil de renseignement, ses instruments de propagande, des cadres terroristes et des forces de combat en Pologne, en Ukraine sovietique et dans d'autres pays" », a-t-elle indique. La porte-parole de la diplomatie russe a souligne que Konovalets avait personnellement rencontre Hitler et qu'il etait « extremement fier » de cette relation personnelle. Elle a rappele que le Führer lui avait propose d'envoyer un groupe de nationalistes ukrainiens etudier dans une ecole du parti nazi a Leipzig. Konovalets est responsable des crimes de l'OUN, affirme Zakharova Maria Zakharova a rappele qu'en reponse a l'assassinat d'un diplomate sovietique a Lvov, organise par l'OUN en 1933, les dirigeants sovietiques avaient pris la decision d'eliminer Konovalets, operation qui avait ete menee a bien le 23 mai 1938. Selon elle, l'elimination de Konovalets a par la suite conduit a une scission de l'Organisation des nationalistes ukrainiens (OUN) entre les partisans de Melnyk et de Bandera, qui ont poursuivi leur cooperation avec le Troisieme Reich. « Konovalets est aussi responsable qu'eux des crimes de l'OUN qu'il a creee », a-t-elle affirme, avant de constater : « Le regime actuel de Kiev a herite de l'ideologie et des methodes des fondateurs de cette organisation criminelle. L'Allemagne figure une fois de plus parmi les principaux parrains du terrorisme ukrainien. » Ce n'est pas le premier nationaliste ukrainien que Kiev a ouvertement exhume pour l'enterrer avec les honneurs sur le territoire ukrainien. En mai dernier, Volodymyr Zelensky a participe a la reinhumation de la depouille d'Andriï Melnyk, l'un des chefs de l'Organisation des nationalistes ukrainiens et de l'Armee insurrectionnelle ukrainienne (UPA), un groupe responsable de crimes de masse et de genocide contre la population civile, commis entre 1943 et 1945 sur les territoires de la Volhynie et de la Galicie orientale. Le chef du regime de Kiev a egalement donne le nom de « Heros de l'UPA » a une unite des forces armees ukrainiennes. Kiev a ensuite essuye de vives critiques de la part de la Pologne, dont la population avait ete victime de massacres perpetres par les nazis ukrainiens. En signe de protestation, le president polonais Karol Nawrocki a retire , le 19 juin, la plus haute distinction polonaise, l'Ordre de l'Aigle blanc, a Volodymyr Zelensky. En outre, debut juin dernier, plus de 30 deputes europeens ont exige que le chef du regime de Kiev soit dechu de sa distinction europeenne.

items.title: Sedina Tamakloe release vindicates NPP’s selective justice concerns – Agyapa Mercer
items.description: Lawyer and member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Andrews Agyapa Mercer, has questioned the fairness of Ghana’s justice system following the release of former Microfinance and Small Loans Centre (MASLOC) Chief Executive Officer, Sedina Christine Tamakloe-Attionu. Speaking on JoyNews’ Top Story on Wednesday, August 12, Mr Mercer said the latest development reinforces concerns that the government is selectively pursuing cases involving political opponents. He said he was not surprised by Ms Tamakloe-Attionu’s release, arguing that the case had followed a pattern he had anticipated since the National Democratic Congress (NDC) assumed office. “I really am not surprised. The script that was formulated when the NDC came into office, commencing with the nolle prosequi that they entered for all persons affiliated with the NDC who were standing trial in the courts,” he said. Mr Mercer noted that although an appeal had been filed as far back as May 2024, no action was taken on it until it was re-listed. He also criticised the Attorney General for failing to file written submissions, saying the office had cited the unavailability of parts of the proceedings at the time. The Court of Appeal subsequently acquitted and discharged Ms Tamakloe-Attionu, after which the Attorney General announced plans to challenge the decision at the Supreme Court. Read also: Sedina Tamakloe released from custody 2 weeks after Court of Appeal acquittal Mr Mercer said the latest development has vindicated concerns raised by some observers about the outcome of the case. “And today, we’ve seen that what people have prophesied has actually come to fruition,” he said. He challenged Ghanaians to determine whether justice had been served or whether the case reflected what he described as a pattern of political victimisation. “It’s for the good people of this country to determine whether, indeed and in fact, the ends of justice have been met, or that it is the usual politics where opponents of the party in office are victimised, taken through the processes of the law, and people who are aligned to the governing party are set free,” he said. Mr Mercer stressed that the NPP does not oppose efforts to hold officials of the previous Akufo-Addo administration accountable for their actions. He, however, argued that accountability must be applied fairly and consistently, regardless of political affiliation. “I have consistently maintained that we, the NPP, are not opposed to people who served in the Akufo-Addo administration being held to account because we believe in the tenets of democracy and the Constitution, which include accountability,” he said. He said concerns arise when the law is applied selectively, creating a perception that members of the governing party are being protected while NPP members are being targeted. “When it’s selective, when there’s cherry-picking, when it’s obvious to everybody that when it comes to some segment of the Ghanaian populace who are affiliated to a particular party… the kinds of things that we’ve seen clearly feed into the perception that this government is out to set the people affiliated to it free, and to hold the NPP people to account,” he added.

items.title: Énergie : l’Algérie conforte son rôle de fournisseur stratégique de GNL pour l'Europe
items.description: La demande des pays europeens en gaz naturel liquefie (GNL) algerien continuera de croître au second semestre 2026, a rapporte le journal l' Algerie Aujourd'hui le 11 août. Selon les auteurs de l'article, cette dynamique s'accompagnera « d'une amelioration des prix qui avoisinent les 60,5 euros/MWh pour les livraisons de septembre, contre 55 euros actuellement ». Selon l'Oxford Institute for Energy Studies, les exportations de gaz algerien par gazoduc vers l'Europe ont progresse de 13 % en mai 2026 par rapport a la meme periode de l'annee precedente. Cette tendance a la hausse s'inscrit dans un contexte de tensions persistantes sur les marches energetiques internationaux. En Europe, notamment, l'une des principales causes est la vague de chaleur qui a mis a rude epreuve le secteur energetique europeen. En juillet dernier, les pays de l'Union europeenne ont ete contraints de prelever 964 millions de metres cubes de gaz sur leurs reserves en raison d'une forte augmentation de la consommation d'electricite. Cette croissance ne se limite toutefois pas au secteur gazier de ce pays africain. L'Algerie a l'intention d' augmenter sa production de petrole dans le cadre de la decision prise le 2 août par les pays de l'OPEP+, selon laquelle sept etats membres du cartel international augmentent leur production collective de 188 000 barils par jour. Selon les previsions, le secteur petrolier algerien devrait depasser en septembre le seuil d'un million de barils par jour, augmentant ainsi sa production de 6 000 barils par jour.

Les Malawiennes ont rapidement pris les commandes de la rencontre grâce à Temwa Chawinga qui a ouvert le score à la 33e minute, avant de doubler la mise dans le temps additionnel de la première période (45e+1). Le Malawi a ainsi regagné les vestiaires avec un avantage confortable de deux buts. Au retour des vestiaires, l’Algérie a trouvé les ressources pour revenir dans la rencontre. Adjali a réduit l’écart à la 60e minute, redonnant espoir aux siennes. Mais le Malawi n’a pas tremblé. Temwa Chawinga a définitivement scellé le sort de la rencontre à la 76e minute, inscrivant son troisième but de la soirée et portant le score à 3-1. items.title: Osun Election: NHRC seeks Fadahunsi’s arrest as Adeyanju writes UK, US for visa ban
items.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA— The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has demanded the immediate suspension and arrest of the Senator for Osun East Senatorial District, Francis Fadahunsi, for allegedly inciting his supporters to kill members of the Accord Party ahead of Saturday’s governorship poll in the state. The Commission, in a statement signed by its Executive Secretary, Chief Tony Ojukwu, SAN, referenced a viral video that captured the lawmaker making statements it said amounted to incitement to murder, electoral violence, and voter intimidation. It urged the police and the Department of State Services (DSS) to arrest, investigate, and prosecute the federal lawmaker. “Senator Fadahunsi is alleged to have instructed supporters to kill members of the Accord Party ahead of Saturday’s Osun governorship election. “In the video circulated online, the person identified as the Senator was translated to have said: ‘From now on, whenever you see Accord members, kill them. I authorise you to kill them. They have wives and children too. This is a Federal Government election. On election day, even if they come with voter cards, we won’t allow them to vote.’ “No well-meaning Nigerian should sit by and allow such rhetoric to be tolerated without consequences from the law enforcement authorities. “This is not politics. This is a licence to kill. A public officer who tells citizens to murder other citizens because of party affiliation must not be allowed to remain in office for one more day. “The Senate leadership is hereby called upon to suspend Senator Fadahunsi immediately, pending conclusive investigation by the police. “The Police and DSS must also arrest, investigate, and prosecute him now. We cannot wait until blood is spilled in Osun before we act. Prevention is the duty of the state, and the leadership of the NASS is part of the state,” the statement added. The NHRC maintained that, given the gravity of the statements attributed to the Senator in the video, the matter required urgent investigation by security agencies under due process. “The Commission is calling on authorities to immediately suspend Senator Fadahunsi from all Senate duties pending investigation. “The Commission urges citizens of Osun to remain peaceful and to report any threats to the Commission and relevant authorities, as it has set up a situation room to report and document such incidents during the election period,” it added. The NHRC’s position came as human rights lawyer Mr. Deji Adeyanju wrote to the United States government and the British High Commission, demanding a visa ban for Senator Fadahunsi and members of his family for actions capable of undermining democratic and electoral processes in Nigeria. “For far too long, Nigerian politicians have acted with impunity in a manner that has subverted the will of the Nigerian people, undermined the rule of law, and caused substantial loss of lives and property of ordinary Nigerians. “We use this medium to urge you to send a strong message to each and every one of them,” Adeyanju stated in his petition. He urged both the US and UK governments to equally consider “the seizure of assets and the foreclosure of business interests of Nigerians who actively undermine the nation’s constitutional democratic process.” The post Osun Election: NHRC seeks Fadahunsi’s arrest as Adeyanju writes UK, US for visa ban appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Bourses 2025-2026 : le paiement des réclamations de novembre à juin a démarré
items.description: La Direction des Bourses, sous tutelle du ministère de l'Enseignement supérieur, de la Recherche et de l'Innovation, a annoncé ce mercredi 12 août le lancement du paiement des réclamations relatives à huit mois de l'année universitaire 2025-2026 : novembre, décembre, janvier, février, mars, avril, mai et juin. Cette opération concerne les étudiants dont les noms figurent déjà sur les états de paiement des mois cités, mais qui n'avaient pas pu percevoir leur bourse en raison de divers blocages administratifs. Trois motifs reviennent principalement : des erreurs de filiation, un numéro de téléphone erroné ou l'expiration du code de retrait. Pour les bénéficiaires souhaitant vérifier leur situation ou obtenir des précisions sur ce règlement, la Direction des Bourses les invite à se rapprocher de SESAPAY, d'ECOBANK, ou directement de ses services, situés rue Docteur Thèze, à Dakar. Le communiqué, signé du Directeur des Bourses Jean Amédé Diatta, marque ainsi un rattrapage attendu par de nombreux étudiants restés sans versement durant plusieurs mois de l'année académique écoulée.

items.title: Osun Election: Accord alleges 29 deaths, seeks EU intervention
items.description: OSOGBO — The Accord Party has appealed to the European Union (EU) to monitor the political situation in Osun State and use its diplomatic influence to promote a peaceful and credible governorship election scheduled for Saturday. The party made the appeal in a letter dated August 12, 2026, and addressed to Gautier Migot, Head of the EU Delegation to Nigeria and ECOWAS. In the letter signed by the National Chairman of the party, Maxwell Mgbudem, Accord alleged that the political atmosphere in the state had deteriorated ahead of the election, citing reports of violence, arrests, intimidation and harassment of political actors and supporters. Mgbudem claimed that at least 29 persons had been killed in incidents allegedly connected with the political situation in the state, while several others were injured. He further alleged that more than 60 members and supporters of the Accord Party had been arrested and detained in Abuja and Nasarawa State. The party chairman also raised concerns over what he described as the selective deployment of federal law enforcement and regulatory institutions during the election period. He, however, stressed that the party was not opposed to legitimate investigations or lawful enforcement actions, but expressed concern about the timing and manner in which such actions were allegedly being carried out. “The timing, manner and perceived selectivity of actions by public institutions during an election period are capable of undermining public confidence if they are not demonstrably impartial, transparent and consistent with due process,” the letter stated. Mgbudem also alleged that Accord members had been subjected to attacks, harassment and intimidation. He cited a viral video in which Senator Francis Fadahunsi was alleged to have called for Accord members to be killed wherever they were found. The senator had previously denied the allegation. Against this backdrop, the Accord chairman urged the EU to take the allegations into consideration and use its diplomatic influence to encourage Nigerian authorities to guarantee a level playing field for all political parties participating in the election. “It is against this background that we respectfully appeal to the European Union delegation to consider using its good offices and diplomatic influence to encourage the immediate de-escalation of the political situation in Osun State,” Mgbudem said. The party also urged the EU to publicly support a free, fair, transparent and peaceful election, with the outcome determined solely by the votes of the electorate. “Specifically, we respectfully request that the European Union publicly reaffirm the importance of a free, fair, transparent, credible, and peaceful election in Osun State, with the outcome determined solely by the freely expressed will of the electorate,” the party stated. Mgbudem said the proposed intervention should focus on preventive diplomacy, arguing that early international engagement could help prevent further escalation of tensions before the election. He added that a timely intervention by the EU would reinforce the need for political competition to remain peaceful, democratic and guided by the rule of law. Abeiku Santana launches Tourism Destination Africa podcast to promote African tourism
items.description: Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA), Gilbert Abeiku Aggrey Santana, has launched a new podcast aimed at amplifying African voices and reshaping global perceptions of the continent’s tourism industry. The podcast, titled Tourism Destination Africa, is designed as an informative, educational and entertaining platform focusing on tourism, travel and hospitality in Ghana and across the continent. Mr Santana, who was recently named among the 2026 Top 100 Most Influential People in Tourism and Hospitality in Africa, said the initiative would provide a platform to explore Africa’s tourism opportunities, cultures and experiences. According to figures released by UN Tourism, Africa welcomed nearly 81 million international visitors in 2025, up from 75.4 million in 2024. The growth made Africa the fastest-growing tourism region globally during the period, ahead of Europe, Asia and the Americas. Despite the growth, Mr Santana said global perceptions of Africa as a tourism destination had not kept pace with the continent’s performance. He cited Ghana’s Year of Return and Beyond the Return initiatives as examples of the country’s ability to attract members of the African diaspora, but stressed the need for sustained storytelling to maintain that momentum. “For as long as many of us can remember, the story of Africa has been told by everyone except Africans,” he said. Mr Santana said Africa’s story had often been framed around colonialism, conflict and hardship, with comparatively less attention given to its achievements, innovation, cultural diversity and tourism potential. He explained that each episode of Tourism Destination Africa would explore a destination, culture, experience or idea deserving of wider recognition. “While some episodes will spotlight lesser-known attractions and communities in Ghana, others will examine tourism developments across the continent and lessons African countries can learn from one another,” he said. The podcast is expected to target tourism professionals, travellers, hospitality stakeholders and audiences interested in how Africa is perceived and represented globally. Mr Santana said the platform would contribute to changing the narrative by giving Africans greater control over how their destinations, cultures and experiences are presented to the world. He encouraged the public to follow the podcast and participate in conversations about the future of tourism on the continent. The initiative comes as African destinations seek to build on recent growth in international arrivals by strengthening destination marketing, cultural storytelling and tourism experiences. items.title: Burkina: un pont sur l’axe routier Banzon-Samorogouan endommagé
items.description: Un pont sur l’axe routier Banzon-Samorogouan a été endommagé à la suite des fortes précipitations enregistrées dans la nuit du 8 au 9 août 2026, selon nos confrères de AIB. Dans la nuit du 8 au 9 août 2026, des pluies tombées ont endommagé un pont sur l’axe routier Bazon-Samorogouan, selon l’agence de presse d’Etat AIB qui souligne que «le Président de la Délégation spéciale (PDS) de Banzon, Sié Poda, s’est rendu sur les lieux dans la matinée du lundi 10 août 2026 afin de constater de visu l’ampleur des dégâts». «Selon les constats effectués, la montée importante des eaux a fragilisé l’ouvrage, provoquant sa détérioration partielle et compromettant la circulation des usagers sur cet axe fréquenté reliant plusieurs localités de la province», rapportent nos confrères. «La protection des infrastructures publiques demeure une priorité. Nous allons engager les démarches nécessaires auprès des structures concernées afin qu’une solution soit trouvée dans les meilleurs délais», a déclaré Sié Poda, cité par AIB. Il a, selon le média d’Etat, «invité les populations et les usagers de la route à faire preuve de vigilance et à respecter les consignes de sécurité, particulièrement en cette période d’hivernage où les fortes pluies peuvent affecter l’état des ouvrages et des voies de communication». Par Wakat Séra L’article Burkina: un pont sur l’axe routier Banzon-Samorogouan endommagé est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Osun Election: PDP accuses APC of treating election as war, blood price for power
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of treating the Osun governorship election as a do-or-die contest, alleging that its rhetoric suggests bloodshed could be the price for retaining political power. The party said the increasingly combative tone around the election was dangerous, stressing that elections should offer citizens a peaceful way to choose their leaders, rather than turn political contests into battles where threats and intimidation overshadow the ballot. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary of the Interim National Working Committee, Ini Ememobong, the PDP demanded an investigation into remarks attributed to Senator Francis Fadahunsi and other alleged threats to a peaceful and transparent election in Osun. “We specifically demand a transparent investigation of the Senator Fadahunsi incident and other threats to peaceful and transparent elections in Osun State,” the party said. The PDP was reacting to a viral video in which Fadahunsi was allegedly heard making a statement about dealing with political opponents before and on election day. “So, we have come to tell you, up till the day of the election, if we see them, it is killing,” Fadahunsi was quoted as saying. The opposition party said the remark was part of a wider pattern of inflammatory rhetoric by the ruling party and its presidential candidate, warning that such language was pushing the country’s political temperature to dangerous levels. “These and many more hurtful rhetorics have been deployed by the ruling party unapologetically, and this has raised the political temperature of the country to unprecedented fever-pitch levels,” the PDP said. It warned that threats, intimidation and attempts to silence opposition voices could erode public confidence in elections and undermine the democratic process. The party called on President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, the APC and its officials to moderate their political communication and ensure that the Osun election is determined by voters rather than fear or coercion. “Civility must take centre stage in our political communication, and the elections must be a true reflection of the will of the people, freely given through the ballot,” it said. The PDP maintained that respecting the choice of voters was essential to preserving the credibility of the election and the survival of democracy. “This is the irreducible minimum, which the government and all political parties must adhere to, in the interest of the survival of democracy and the country,” the party said. The post Osun Election: PDP accuses APC of treating election as war, blood price for power appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has raised the alarm over an alleged plan to arrest its National Secretary, Rauf Aregbesola, ahead of Saturday’s governorship election in Osun State. The party, in a statement issued on Wednesday by its National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, said it had received what it described as “credible reports” of moves to arrest the former Osun State governor in the days leading to the poll. The ADC expressed concern that such an action could be intended to disrupt its campaign and election-day activities, particularly Aregbesola’s role in coordinating the party’s efforts. “Given the pattern of intimidation, harassment and misuse of state institutions that has increasingly characterised the conduct of this government towards the opposition, we cannot afford to dismiss these reports,” Abdullahi said. Aregbesola, who governed Osun between 2010 and 2018 and later served as Minister of the Interior, is currently the national secretary of the opposition party. The ADC said any invitation by security agencies should follow due process, given Aregbesola’s political status and previous public offices. “Ogbeni Aregbesola is a former Governor of Osun State, a former Minister of the Federal Republic and the National Secretary of the opposition political party. If any security agency has a lawful reason to invite him, there are established procedures for doing so,” the party said. It warned that arresting him shortly before the election could be interpreted as an attempt to weaken the party’s participation in the poll. “An arrest on the eve of an election in which his party is participating would invite only one reasonable conclusion: that the purpose is to prevent him from leading and coordinating the party’s election activities,” the statement added. The opposition party consequently urged the Federal Government and security agencies to avoid actions capable of undermining the credibility of the election. “The eyes of Nigerians are on Osun,” Abdullahi said, urging authorities to uphold democratic principles. “Whatever happens before, during and after Saturday’s election will be judged not by the explanations offered afterwards, but by the actions taken now.” The ADC also called on the APC-led Federal Government to avoid measures that could heighten political tension in the state. “Nigeria is still a democracy, and the government would do well to remember that before Saturday,” Abdullahi said. items.title: Liverpool, Manchester United, Chelsea : la bataille anglaise s’intensifie autour de Lamine Camara
items.description: Le milieu sénégalais de l'AS Monaco n'en finit plus de faire tourner les têtes outre-Manche. Après Crystal Palace, Nottingham Forest, Manchester United et Liverpool, c'est désormais Chelsea qui s'invite officiellement dans le dossier Lamine Camara, selon les informations de Foot Mercato relayées ces dernières heures. Cinq clubs de Premier League suivent de près le natif de Niaguis, à trois ans de la fin programmée de son idylle avec le club du Rocher. Crystal Palace a dégainé le premier, avec une offre autour de 35 millions de livres déjà repoussée par la direction monégasque. Une proposition jugée trop timide au regard des ambitions affichées par l'ASM, qui évalue son milieu à hauteur de 50 millions d'euros, soit près de 33 milliards de francs CFA. Chelsea, de son côté, ne cache plus son intérêt mais avance avec prudence. Les Blues devront d'abord dégraisser leur entrejeu, en se séparant d'un ou deux éléments, avant d'espérer formuler une offre à la hauteur des attentes monégasques. Un scénario qui n'a rien d'anodin pour un club abonné aux emplettes tonitruantes ces dernières saisons sur le marché français. Liverpool et Newcastle, déjà cités depuis le printemps comme prétendants sérieux, complètent ce tableau où Manchester United et Nottingham Forest ne sont pas en reste. Une source proche du dossier évoquait récemment un profil scruté pour sa constance, sa maturité et sa capacité à tenir un tempo élevé sur toute une rencontre – les qualités précises qui ont convaincu plusieurs recruteurs anglais de passer à l'action. Sous contrat jusqu'en 2029 et dépourvu de clause libératoire, Camara place Monaco en position de force. Le club de la Principauté, fidèle à sa politique de formation-revente qui avait déjà permis d’empocher 80 millions d'euros lors du départ d'Aurélien Tchouaméni vers le Real Madrid, n'a aucune urgence à vendre. Seule une offre jugée « astronomique », entre 65 et 75 millions d'euros selon plusieurs sources anglaises, pourrait faire vaciller la position de la direction rocheronne.

items.title: Sedina case: There’s nothing to appeal – Amaliba on AG’s decision to withdraw stay application
items.description: Former Director of Legal Affairs of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Abraham Amaliba, has suggested that the Attorney-General may have withdrawn the application seeking to keep former MASLOC Chief Executive Sedina Tamakloe-Attionu in custody after concluding that there was little basis to pursue the matter. According to him, the Attorney-General may have reviewed the Court of Appeal’s judgment and determined that an appeal to the Supreme Court was unlikely to succeed. Mr Amaliba was commenting on the decision by the Attorney-General to withdraw the stay of execution application following the Court of Appeal’s acquittal and discharge of Ms Tamakloe-Attionu. The Court of Appeal on July 30, 2026, unanimously overturned her conviction and 10-year prison sentence, holding that the prosecution had failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. Speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story on August 12, Mr Amaliba said the withdrawal could be explained by the Attorney-General’s approach to prosecutions, which he said is based on the availability and strength of evidence. “I can only hazard a guess,” he said when asked why the Attorney-General withdrew the stay of application processes filed. “Don’t forget that the appeal was filed at the time when the judgment was not before the Attorney-General. You remember he said that in his press conference. He said that this morning, that was when he was speaking, that he has a soft copy; he has not read it yet, but he has ordered the DPP. “I’m sure after reading it, he comes to the firm conclusion that there’s nothing to appeal, and that when you appeal, you will lose.” Mr Amaliba noted that the Attorney-General has previously maintained that prosecutions should only be pursued where there is sufficient evidence to support them. He said it was therefore possible that a review of the appellate court’s judgment influenced the decision to withdraw the stay application. The Attorney-General had initially directed the Director of Public Prosecutions to file a notice of appeal at the Supreme Court and an application for a stay of execution of the Court of Appeal’s judgment. The State had argued that the Court of Appeal’s decision contained errors of law and fact and that there were substantial grounds for the Supreme Court to overturn it. It also expressed concern that Ms Tamakloe-Attionu could leave the jurisdiction before the Supreme Court determined the appeal. However, following the withdrawal of the stay application, a judge signed the release warrant for Ms Tamakloe-Attionu, paving the way for her release from custody. Mr Amaliba also rejected suggestions from the opposition NPP that the development vindicated its earlier claims that the government intended to shield Ms Tamakloe-Attionu. He argued that such claims ignored the independence of the judiciary and the effect of the Court of Appeal’s ruling.

items.title: AOC Knows a Lemon When She Sees One
items.description: Last night, Francesca Hong lost the race to be the Democratic candidate for governor of Wisconsin. This is great news for American democracy. Sorry if that seems harsh—she certainly ran an energetic campaign and came close to winning the nomination—but Hong was a profoundly flawed candidate in an important race. Even the leaders of her own faction of the Democratic Party recognized it, and stayed away: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Bernie Sanders apparently know a lemon when they see one. Her narrow loss is a positive reflection on the progressive luminaries’ judgment, as well as a demonstration that the party mainstream eventually managed to sort out a messy and dispiriting primary. The Democrats now have a better chance of winning a crucial swing state’s governorship, against a Republican nominee who, while in Congress, went along with Donald Trump’s efforts to overturn the 2020 election. Hong’s loss yesterday was unexpected. Two weeks ago, the 37-year-old state legislator was the front-runner in the polls, largely because the Democratic primary had turned into a clown show. One mainstream candidate, Lieutenant Governor Sara Rodriguez, suspended her campaign in mid-July because of financial irregularities. By the end of the month, with less than a fortnight to go before Election Day, former Lieutenant Governor Mandela Barnes bowed out too. At the time he did so, one poll had Hong 22 points ahead . In the interim, another candidate, Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, had returned to the race after previously withdrawing because of a lack of momentum. All the hopes of the Democratic establishment rested on Crowley’s Hail Mary pass. Why were they so scared of Hong? Partially because she is a member of the Democratic Socialists of America, an organization that calls for public ownership of large corporations, looser immigration laws, and the abolition of prisons. Hong has said that she does not agree with all of the DSA platform, but she entered the contest with an unscrubbed Twitter account, full of the most voter-repelling, peak-2020 statements you can imagine. In the COVID era, when joyless leftist platitudes were all the rage, she criticized Thanksgiving as a “colonizer holiday” and “the original superspreader event that killed Indegenous [ sic ] folx and women.” (Wait, does folx —a baffling attempt to make the already gender-neutral word folks even more inclusive—not include women?) Further searches of her Twitter account revealed that she also disliked Christmas, Valentine’s Day, and even Halloween, which she said was “not my thing.” [ Read: America’s most divided state loves its extremes ] A savvier candidate than Hong might have been able to muscle through the inevitable criticism with an AOC-style acknowledgment that “Woke 1 was crazy.” We all lost our minds a bit during the pandemic shutdown: Remember when Gal Gadot and other celebrities posted that video of themselves singing “Imagine”? But Hong could not manage to distance herself from her comments back then. In what could have been her cleanup operation, an interview with CNN’s Kaitlan Collins, she explained that “Thanksgiving is also a time that’s incredibly painful for many people in our communities.” (For the turkey community, definitely.) She clarified a few days later that “I actually love it,” but that she was “kind of a curmudgeon when it comes to holidays in general.” The problem wasn’t just her previous statements, but her inability to back out gracefully from her own rhetorical cul-de-sac. Despite the buoyant polling, I suspected that Hong was doomed after attending a rally she held in suburban Milwaukee earlier this month. She has an appealing backstory—restaurant worker, single mom, community organizer—and, as I saw from the rally, Korean immigrant parents who were proud as punch to see their daughter running for office. They sat right at the front, behind the television cameras, beaming throughout. Sadly, though, she also had a nervous, rabbity speaking style. At her own event, she looked like the support act to the left-wing streamer Hasan Piker, who said in 2019 that America deserved 9/11, and who had turned up to read a short encomium to socialism from his iPhone. Afterward, she milled around uncertainly while he posed for selfies with a crowd that hungrily pressed against the security barrier. Apart from their other skills, politicians need a bit of main-character energy. Abdul El-Sayed, the left-wing Senate candidate in Michigan, also carries a lot of baggage—his Muslim faith and Arab name, his advocacy for universal health care, some loose-lipped podcasts in his past—and, like Hong, he has campaigned alongside Piker. But in person, El-Sayed comes off as eloquent, combative, and focused. He is not going to spend the next three months talking about which national holidays he hates most. He also looks comfortable in all kinds of settings: appearing with his white step-grandparents in a campaign ad, campaigning against data centers alongside rural farmers, sparring with TV anchors over U.S. policy toward Israel. And he has boiled down his campaign to a simple three-part slogan: “Money out of politics, money in your pocket, Medicare for All . ” El-Sayed is a risky candidate, for sure, but a blue wave might well carry him into the Senate. That was not true for Hong. Swing voters? Never heard of them. Her campaign rally was pure crack for disaffected leftist Millennials. The emcee introduced every speech by appealing to “ladies, gentlemen, and friends beyond the binary,” while the back of the hall featured an activity zone with blank sheets of paper and crayons. Her volunteer-made campaign pins had slogans such as STONERS FOR HONG and FUCK ICE . If the offerings at the merch store were any indication, her most memorable campaign moment up to that point had come at a community grill, where she flipped burgers and told a bystander: “Reagan fucked us, Paul.” The group of 20-somethings behind me were wearing this slogan on their T-shirts. The crowd at the rally was enthusiastic and idealistic, and Hong might have gotten away with such an event in deep-blue Manhattan, but not in a state that Donald Trump won in 2024. Notably, Ocasio-Cortez and Sanders were happy to endorse and campaign for El-Sayed, but neither of them gave their blessing to Hong. Neither did Elizabeth Warren. (“I don’t know her,” the senator from Massachusetts said recently, as if channeling the famous Mariah Carey meme .) The left wing of the Democratic Party has had a great primary season, with unexpected wins in New York and even Colorado . But the refusal of its leading figures to endorse a subpar candidate in a purple state suggests that they are being judicious about where they put their time and on whom they stake their reputation. Ocasio-Cortez also declined to endorse Graham Platner, a progressive favorite whose campaign for the Senate in Maine imploded amid allegations of sexual misconduct. With candidates, quality control is everything. [ Idrees Kahloon: The Democrats can’t just laugh off ‘Woke 1’ ] In a last-minute intervention, outgoing Governor Tony Evers—who had pledged to stay out of the race—explicitly endorsed Crowley when the latter relaunched his campaign. The gambit worked. Crowley squeaked past Hong at the last minute. That is a nightmare for the Republicans, whose candidate Tom Tiffany was the only serious contender for the party’s nomination. In Congress, he is a member of the hard-right Freedom Caucus and voted against certifying Joe Biden’s victory in 2020. He has been heartily endorsed by Donald Trump—great for the primary, but worse than useless in the general. Tiffany very obviously wanted to run against Hong, whom he could have painted as a dangerous radical who loves illegal immigration and hates cranberry sauce. Her campaign spent virtually nothing on television advertising, while a super PAC linked to Republicans invested $2.2 million in ads depicting her as too liberal, in what the Times called “a counterintuitive strategy to grow her appeal among Democratic primary voters.” If anyone heard a loud thump in Madison last night, that was the sound of a huge opposition-research file hitting a trash can. The final winner, however, is democracy itself. Who would bet against Donald Trump calling up swing-state officials in 2028 and asking them to find a few more votes for the Republican candidate for president? After all, that’s exactly what he did in Georgia in 2020. Joe Biden won Wisconsin by just 21,000 votes that year, while Trump took it back by only 30,000 in the next race. For a decade, Trump and his allies have counted on Democrats to sound so out of step with mainstream voters on cultural issues that even his most authoritarian moves look tolerable by comparison. The Badger State is one of the most crucial places on the electoral map. Francesca Hong’s unexpected loss is America’s gain.

items.title: Éclipse solaire : les bons réflexes pour observer le phénomène sans danger
items.description: Une éclipse solaire constitue un phénomène astronomique spectaculaire, susceptible de susciter la curiosité de nombreux observateurs. Mais si le rendez-vous céleste peut être admiré, il ne doit surtout pas l’être au mépris des précautions nécessaires. À l’occasion de l’éclipse solaire, le ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique appelle les populations à protéger leurs yeux et à redoubler de vigilance, notamment à l’égard des enfants. Le Soleil, un danger pour les yeux Contrairement à une idée répandue, la diminution apparente de la luminosité du Soleil pendant une éclipse ne le rend pas moins dangereux pour la vision. Regarder directement le Soleil, même brièvement et sans protection adaptée, peut provoquer des lésions importantes de la rétine. La particularité de ces atteintes est qu’elles peuvent apparaître sans douleur immédiate. Dans certains cas, elles peuvent entraîner une baisse de la vision susceptible d’être irréversible. Des équipements adaptés indispensables Pour observer directement une éclipse, les autorités sanitaires recommandent exclusivement l’utilisation de lunettes spécialement conçues pour l’observation des éclipses solaires et conformes aux normes de sécurité en vigueur. Les lunettes de soleil classiques, même très foncées, ne constituent pas une protection suffisante. Il est également déconseillé d’utiliser des solutions improvisées telles que les verres teintés, les films photographiques, les radiographies ou d’autres filtres artisanaux. Une vigilance particulière est également requise avec les instruments optiques. Jumelles, télescopes, appareils photo et autres dispositifs ne doivent jamais être utilisés pour regarder le Soleil sans un filtre solaire spécifiquement adapté. Les enfants particulièrement concernés Les enfants doivent faire l’objet d’une surveillance accrue pendant le phénomène. Il est recommandé de leur expliquer les risques liés à l’observation directe du Soleil et de les accompagner s’ils souhaitent suivre l’éclipse. Pour les personnes qui ne disposent pas d’un équipement répondant aux exigences de sécurité, le choix le plus prudent reste de ne pas regarder directement le Soleil. Rester attentif après l’éclipse La vigilance doit se poursuivre après le phénomène. Une atteinte rétinienne peut ne provoquer aucune douleur au moment de l’exposition. Certains symptômes peuvent toutefois apparaître dans les heures qui suivent : vision floue, baisse de la vision, apparition d’une tache sombre ou d’une zone floue au centre du champ visuel, déformation des images ou sensibilité inhabituelle à la lumière. En cas d’apparition de l’un de ces signes après avoir regardé le Soleil, il est recommandé de consulter rapidement un professionnel de santé spécialisé en ophtalmologie. L’éclipse ne dure que quelques instants, mais les dommages qu’une observation imprudente peut provoquer sur la vision peuvent, eux, être durables. La prudence reste donc la meilleure manière de profiter de ce spectacle astronomique.

items.title: Labé : Un «fou » interpellé avec des dollars et plusieurs téléphones
items.description: Portant des habits usés et faisant croire à des troubles mentaux, un homme aux agissements suspects a été arrêté ce mercredi 12 août à Labé en possession de 700 dollars américains et de plusieurs téléphones. Pris en chasse par la vigilance des citoyens, le suspect est désormais au cœur d'une enquête d'une sensibilité inattendue, a appris la rédaction régionale de Guinéenews basée à Labé. C’est une scène pour le moins inhabituelle qui s’est déroulée à quelques mètres seulement du commissariat central de police de Labé, au carrefour Tinkisso. Un individu au profil énigmatique, que beaucoup prenaient jusqu'ici pour un simple déficient mental, a été interpellé ce mercredi 12 août 2026 par les agents de la police centrale. La vigilance des chauffeurs de taxi-moto de la zone a été le facteur déclencheur. Intrigués par le comportement suspect de l'homme, ces derniers ont commencé à l'encercler et à s'interroger ouvertement sur ses faits et gestes. Sentant le piège se refermer et redoutant la vindicte populaire, l'inconnu a préféré se réfugier de lui-même auprès des forces de l'ordre. La fouille de ses effets personnels a révélé une surprise de taille : sous ses vêtements usés, l'homme dissimulait la somme de 700 dollars américains, plusieurs téléphones portables et divers objets. Cette arrestation ravive de sombres souvenirs dans la cité de Karamoko Alpha. Selon les informations recueillies par nos reporters, l'individu n'en est pas à son coup d'essai. Il avait déjà été appréhendé il y a quelque temps aux alentours de la gare routière de Kouroula pour une affaire de vol. Mory Diakité, secrétaire général du syndicat des taxis-motos USTG (union syndicale des travailleurs de Guinée) de Labé, se souvient très bien de cet épisode : « À l'époque, il avait été saisi avec un lot d'objets suspects, dont de nombreuses cartes SIM. Malheureusement, tout le monde avait conclu qu'il s'agissait d'un fou et il avait été libéré sans que l'on cherche à comprendre comment il s'était procuré toutes ces puces », déplore-t-il. Si le commissariat central de Labé se refuse pour l'instant à tout commentaire officiel, l'affaire a pris une tournure judiciaire et politique majeure. Selon des sources concordantes, le procureur près le tribunal de première instance (TPI) de Labé ainsi que sa hiérarchie ont immédiatement été saisis. Plus évocateur encore : le dossier serait suivi de très près jusqu'au niveau de la Présidence de la République. Aux dernières nouvelles, dès la fin des enquêtes préliminaires menées par les services locaux, le suspect devrait être transféré sous haute escorte vers Conakry pour la suite des investigations. Dans la ville de Labé, l'incompréhension laisse place aux spéculations : s'agit-il d'un réseau d'espionnage, de grand banditisme ou de trafic organisé utilisant la folie comme couverture ? Les résultats de l'enquête sont attendus dans les jours à venir. A suivre

items.title: AJK polls: Rathore’s LA-17 Haveli victory disputed, local PML-N announces indefinite strike
items.description: MUZAFFARABAD: A controversy emerged on Wednesday after the returning officer (RO) issued Form 27 declaring PPP’s Faisal Mumtaz Rathore, the sitting AJK prime minister, the winner from LA-17 (Haveli), despite rival PML-N candidate Engineer Mohsin Aziz being assured that the form would not be issued until the Election Commission took up his complaint. The development triggered fresh tensions in Haveli district, where PML-N workers announced a complete shutter-down strike and protest from Thursday (August 13) for an indefinite period. At a meeting in Forward Kahuta, chaired by PML-N Haveli president Syed Abid Bukhari, participants demanded that the Election Commission open all polling bags from LA-17, order a recount and determine the result on the basis of the original results issued by presiding officers at the polling stations. They warned that the scope of the protest would be expanded if the demand was not accepted. Polling in the constituency had been held on Monday amid serious allegations and counter-allegations of rigging by all three major contestants — PM Rathore of PPP, PML-N’s Aziz and independent candidate Khawaja Tariq Saeed. Late on Monday evening, thousands of Aziz’s supporters gathered at the district courts, claiming that the results provided to polling agents by presiding officers on Form 24 showed their candidate leading Rathore by more than 8,000 votes, but that the RO was subsequently preparing the result in favour of the prime minister. There were also reports of some people being injured during the demonstration. The protest ended on Tuesday after Aziz said in a video message that the RO had given him a written undertaking that Form 27 would not be issued until the Election Commission in Muzaffarabad decided his claim. On Tuesday, Chief Election Commissioner Justice (retd) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal had told Dawn that the Commission would take a decision after the polling bags and relevant election records reached its office. He had reportedly given a similar assurance to Aziz over the phone. The DRO, Waheed Mughal, and RO, Asheer Chughtai, both members of the subordinate judiciary, were evacuated from their offices in Forward Kahuta along with the polling bags with the help of the army’s Quick Response Force (QRF). They reached Muzaffarabad by midnight. However, the RO subsequently issued Form 27 after midnight, dated August 11, declaring Rathore the winner with 33,872 votes. Aziz secured 32,354 votes, followed by Saeed with 12,538 and IPP candidate Amir Nazir Chaudhry with 5,405. Hours later, PM Rathore said on X that his “remarkable victory had been officially notified”. “LA-17 has spoken. I thank the people of Haveli and again pledge to serve them now and forever. I’m grateful to my party leadership, specially, Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari and Adi Faryal Talpur, for their trust, guidance and unending support amid every challenge we have faced,” he wrote. The issuance of Form 27, however, failed to settle the dispute, with reports from Haveli suggesting that tensions were rising again. In a video message recorded in Muzaffarabad, Aziz reiterated his allegation that the Form 24s handed to polling agents of all nine participating candidates contained the genuine results, while different figures were subsequently taken into consideration by the RO. He offered to have just two polling bags, rather than all of them, opened from areas where he alleged the results had been changed. If his allegation proved to be wrong, he said, he would apologise and congratulate Rathore. “If Faisal Rathore has won, why is he afraid of opening of polling bags and a subsequent recount?” he asked. Aziz also claimed that the Election Act, 2020, made it obligatory for the RO to open polling bags following a complaint by any candidate. He said that when they asked Chughtai to take the step, the RO maintained that he was unaware of the provision and did not have a copy of the Act with him. On Wednesday, senior lawyers Raja Sajjad Ahmed and Chaudhry Ghulam Nabi submitted an application to the chief election commissioner, seeking a recount of votes polled in LA-17 over alleged tampering with the results. The Election Commission announced that it would take up the matter at 10am on Thursday. In a post on X, PML-N leader and federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry called for a transparent investigation into the rigging complaint filed by Aziz, saying he hoped the Election Commission would address the allegations regarding the Haveli constituency on merit. Aziz, however, said he had little hope from the commission after what he described as its failure to prevent the issuance of the “unlawful Form 27”. “I will take my case to the people’s court apart from the superior judiciary,” he said. Meanwhile, Saeed also alleged tampering with his results and called for a recount. He claimed that he had won at nine polling stations, but the votes secured by him there had not been included in his tally and had instead been added to that of Rathore. PPP calls polls ‘rigged and violent’ Against this backdrop, the PPP also criticised the conduct of the AJK elections, with a high-level meeting of the party in Islamabad describing the polls as “rigged and violent” and expressing serious concern over the role of the AJK Election Commission. The meeting, chaired by PPP Women’s Wing president and AJK affairs in-charge Faryal Talpur, also criticised the phase-wise conduct of the elections and demanded the immediate completion of polling in the remaining two districts of the third phase and seven constituencies of Poonch so that the Legislative Assembly could be fully constituted. The participants raised questions over the suspension of internet services, shortages of polling material and staff at some polling stations, and alleged inadequate security arrangements. Talpur said the PPP was the representative party of the people of AJK and had continued to enjoy strong public support despite challenging circumstances. On the other hand, Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said the PML-N had secured a clear lead in the elections and would have 24 general seats, with another six reserved seats, taking its strength to 30. In his post on X, he said the AJK Assembly session would be convened next week for the swearing-in of members and election of reserved seats, followed by elections for the speaker and prime minister. Chaudhry described the elections as free, fair and credible, saying there had been “zero tolerance” for misconduct or rigging. He cited the arrest of a candidate in LA-6 (Mirpur) for taking away a ballot box from a polling station as an example of action against electoral misconduct.

items.title: Hamdallah et Ronaldo à la poursuite d’Al-Somah : la bataille des buteurs s’annonce explosive
items.description: À quelques jours du coup d’envoi de la 19e saison du championnat saoudien, la course au titre de meilleur buteur historique promet déjà d’être passionnante. En tête depuis plusieurs années, le Syrien Omar Al-Somah voit le Marocain Abderrazak Hamdallah se rapprocher dangereusement, tandis que Cristiano Ronaldo continue de grimper dans la hiérarchie. Le championnat saoudien ne se joue pas uniquement pour le titre. À chaque saison, les stars de la Saudi Pro League se livrent également une bataille acharnée pour inscrire leur nom dans l’histoire de la compétition. Et dans cette course, Abderrazak Hamdallah est le principal poursuivant d’Omar Al-Somah. L’ancien attaquant d’Al-Ahli et d’Al-Hilal reste le meilleur buteur de l’histoire du championnat saoudien avec 161 réalisations. Mais son record est désormais sérieusement menacé par l’international marocain. Auteur de 156 buts en championnat saoudien, Hamdallah n’est plus qu’à cinq longueurs d’Al-Somah. Le Marocain, aujourd’hui attaquant de Al-Taawoun FC, pourrait donc s’emparer du record dès cette saison s’il conserve son efficacité devant le but. Arrivé en Arabie saoudite en 2018, Hamdallah s’est rapidement imposé comme l’un des attaquants les plus prolifiques de l’histoire de la Saudi Pro League. Son instinct dans la surface et sa régularité lui permettent aujourd’hui de viser un nouveau record individuel. Derrière le Marocain, une autre superstar continue de faire parler ses statistiques : Cristiano Ronaldo. Le capitaine d’Al-Nassr compte désormais 102 buts en championnat saoudien. Il a atteint ce total lors de la dernière journée de la saison passée, face à Damac. En seulement quelques saisons, le Portugais a donc déjà intégré le cercle très fermé des joueurs ayant inscrit plus de 100 buts dans la compétition. À l’aube de cette nouvelle saison, tous les regards seront donc tournés vers Abderrazak Hamdallah. Avec seulement cinq buts à inscrire pour égaler Al-Somah, puis six pour devenir le meilleur buteur de l’histoire du championnat saoudien, l’attaquant marocain a une occasion en or d’entrer définitivement dans la légende. Et derrière lui, Cristiano Ronaldo poursuit sa propre ascension. La nouvelle saison pourrait ainsi offrir une bataille spectaculaire entre plusieurs générations de buteurs. The post Hamdallah et Ronaldo à la poursuite d’Al-Somah : la bataille des buteurs s’annonce explosive appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Voter apathy: Youth silence is killing democracy — PDP
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, has warned that voter apathy among young Nigerians is weakening the country’s democracy, urging youths to convert their numerical strength into electoral power by actively participating in elections and governance. The warning came yesterday in Abuja at the party’s 2026 International Youth Day programme, where speakers said young Nigerians could no longer afford to remain spectators in decisions shaping their future. They identified voter apathy, unemployment, economic hardship and the high cost of political participation as major obstacles to youth involvement. Delivering the keynote address, PDP National Director of Administration, Arthur Ekwelem, said Nigeria’s youths had the numbers, energy, creativity and digital influence to transform the electoral landscape. “Democracy thrives on participation. When citizens withdraw from the electoral process, they surrender part of their democratic power to others,” Ekwelem said. He identified distrust in political leaders and institutions, fear of electoral violence, economic hardship, misinformation, inadequate civic education and logistical difficulties among the factors discouraging citizens from voting. Representing the Chairman of the occasion, former Jigawa State governor, Sule Lamido, the PDP Gombe governorship candidate, Isah Pantami, said youths, who constitute more than 60 per cent of Nigeria’s population, must have a stronger voice in policymaking and governance. “They are the backbone of our humanity. They are the vanguards of any positive change. They are the ambassadors of progress and development,” Pantami said. He listed opportunities in the creative industry, digital economy, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, smart agriculture and other emerging sectors, but said unemployment, an outdated education system, inadequate mentorship and the rising cost of living were limiting young Nigerians. Pantami also criticised the gap between the ‘Not Too Young To Run’ principle and the realities of seeking elective office, saying nomination fees, campaigns and other election expenses had made political participation difficult for many youths. “Not too young to run … is only about an academic work where we have a law in place,” he said. Director-General of the PDP Female Youth Wing, Hon. Loveth Izekor, urged young women to move beyond being mobilised for elections and become decision-makers. “Democracy dies when youth are silent. We must move from being mobilised to being decision-makers,” Izekor said. She called for greater access to political funding, training and tickets for young women, saying the gathering was intended as a strategy session rather than merely a celebration. PDP National Youth Leader, Amb. Ibrahim Bala-Aboki, said his office had focused on youth mobilisation, inclusion and grassroots participation since assuming office, including mobilising young members for party congresses, INEC e-registration and elective positions. He said the PDP had also inaugurated a National Youth Leadership Consultative Forum and commenced the revalidation of youth support groups nationwide. Bala-Aboki announced a skills programme to train 100 youths as trainers, with each expected to train 50 youths across the country’s 774 local government areas in vocational and entrepreneurial skills. “This is the time for action, not docility; time for valued alacrity, not void alarms; time for greater momentum, not murmurs,” he said. He urged young Nigerians to reject voter apathy, insisting that their numerical strength could determine the direction of Nigerian democracy. “Every voter is a leader. Together, let us shape and forge our chosen future,” Bala-Aboki said. The post Voter apathy: Youth silence is killing democracy — PDP appeared first on Vanguard News .
