items.title: BoG Governor urges banks to redesign loans for agriculture-focused SMEs
items.description: The Governor of the Bank of Ghana (BoG), Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama, has urged banks to develop more innovative and flexible credit products tailored to the needs of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), particularly businesses operating along the agricultural value chain. He said despite the improvement in Ghana’s economic conditions and a strong rebound in credit creation, many SMEs in the agricultural sector continue to struggle to access financing because banks perceive them as relatively high-risk businesses. Dr Asiama made the call when he engaged Chief Executive Officers and heads of banks, where he outlined recent developments in the economy and the banking sector. “However, despite the improved economic environment and the growing demand for credit, many SMEs, particularly those on the agricultural value chain, still struggle to access finance, just because banks continue to perceive these businesses as relatively high risk,” he said. The Governor argued that banks must move beyond traditional lending approaches and develop a better understanding of the sectors and businesses they finance. “As banks, you are not merely financial intermediaries, you are important business partners in the growth and transformation of the economy,” Dr Asiama stated. He specifically urged banks to design loan products that reflect the seasonal nature of agricultural businesses, particularly in determining repayment schedules. “This should include developing innovative and flexible credit products that recognise the seasonal nature of agricultural activities and align loan repayment schedules with the timing and pattern of borrowers’ cash flows,” he said. According to the Governor, such an approach would make it easier for SMEs to secure financing under conditions that reflect the realities of their operations. “Such an approach would enable SMEs to access financing on terms that better reflect the realities of their businesses,” he added. The call comes as financial conditions in Ghana continue to ease, with the Bank of Ghana reporting a significant rebound in credit creation. Private sector credit grew by 41.2% in June 2026, compared with 8.6% recorded in the same period a year earlier, while real private sector credit growth stood at 34.1%. Dr Asiama said the improvement in financial conditions provides an opportunity for banks to increase their support for productive sectors of the economy. He noted that interest rates in the money market have continued to moderate across various market segments, with these developments beginning to translate into stronger credit flows to the private sector. The Governor also pointed to broader improvements in the banking sector, including stronger capitalisation and asset quality. The industry’s capital adequacy ratio increased to 20.4% in June 2026, from 10.6% a year earlier, while the non-performing loan ratio declined to 16.1% from 23.1% over the same period. With agriculture employing a significant proportion of businesses and households and serving as a key source of raw materials for industry, Dr Asiama’s call places renewed emphasis on ensuring that improved financial conditions translate into greater access to productive credit.

items.title: Osun Election: Ex-PDP guber aspirant endorses Adeleke
items.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo OSOGBO — A former governorship aspirant of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Osun State, Mr Adebayo Adedamola, popularly known as Fryo, has endorsed Governor Ademola Adeleke for the August 15, 2026 governorship election. Adedamola was nominated by a faction of the PDP for the election and polled 919 out of 957 votes at the party’s primary held in Osogbo, the state capital. However, his name was not included in the final list of candidates for the election released by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Adedamola, alongside his supporters, announced his endorsement of Adeleke on Wednesday at a press conference in Osogbo, saying the decision followed extensive consultations, sober reflection and an assessment of the political situation in the state. He said: “I have arrived at this decision based on my assessment of the political circumstances in our state and my conviction that, at this particular moment, this is the direction I am prepared to support. “I encourage all PDP members, supporters and party structures across the state who believe in my leadership and judgment to support the emergence of His Excellency, Senator Ademola Adeleke, at the August 15 gubernatorial election.” The PDP chieftain said he remained proud of his participation in the party’s primary and expressed appreciation to those who supported his candidacy. He, however, said politics involved making difficult decisions at critical moments, stressing that the larger interest of the people should take precedence over personal ambition. “Politics is not only about contesting elections. Politics is also about understanding the realities of the moment, making difficult decisions when necessary, and putting the larger interest of our people above personal ambition,” he said. Adedamola added that he had communicated his decision to PDP leaders, members and stakeholders across the state. Ahead of Saturday’s election, he called for a peaceful poll and urged political leaders, candidates and their supporters to reject violence, intimidation and hate speech. “Osun State is bigger than any individual. Osun State is bigger than any political party. And Osun State is certainly bigger than any election. “We must allow the people to exercise their democratic rights freely and peacefully,” he said. He urged PDP members and party structures across the state to work towards the re-election of Adeleke while conducting themselves lawfully and responsibly. items.title: Black Queens demand outstanding bonuses and better support from government
items.description: Ghana’s senior women’s national team, the Black Queens, have demanded the payment of outstanding bonuses and per diems while accusing the government of neglect and inadequate professional support during their campaign at the ongoing Women’s Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco. The Black Queens exited the competition at the quarterfinal stage after a 2-1 defeat to Malawi, a result that ended Ghana’s hopes of securing an automatic qualification spot for next year’s FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. In a statement issued ahead of their World Cup playoff against Côte d’Ivoire on Thursday, the players expressed frustration over what they described as a general lack of support and called for improved treatment and better professional conditions in future national team assignments. The players expressed disappointment at the level of official support during their WAFCON campaign, noting that the Sports Minister and President were present only at their first official training session. Despite their concerns, the Black Queens stressed that the statement was not intended to create conflict or disrespect anyone, but rather to demand “transparency, accountability, fairness and respect.” They also praised their technical staff for standing by them throughout the campaign and urged the relevant authorities to engage with the players and work towards a swift resolution. The players also called for their outstanding financial obligations to be settled, while urging the relevant authorities to provide the necessary support to enable the team to compete at the highest level. Ghana will face Côte d’Ivoire on Thursday with a place in the World Cup playoffs at stake.

items.title: Some Ghanaians have a way of boxing you – Perez Musik
items.description: Award-winning gospel musician Perez Musik has criticised the tendency to place Ghanaian artistes in fixed musical categories, saying musicians should be allowed to explore different sounds without being defined by a single genre. Speaking on The Career Trail on Joy Learning TV and Joy News, he said he faced difficulties both when urban gospel was not widely accepted within Christian circles and later when he began experimenting with contemporary sounds. “One of the challenges was that it’s not really an accepted genre in the country. The Christian fraternity hasn’t come to terms with that aspect of the song ministry. So it was quite difficult,” he said. Perez Musik explained that urban gospel provided an avenue for young Christians to express their faith through music that connected with their generation. He later encountered a different form of resistance when he began exploring contemporary music. “One of the challenges I faced when I say, in quotes, ‘transition’, was that the people in the contemporary side were like, ‘Ah, who’s this? Is he part of us? Is he one of us? Where’s he coming from?’” he said. He stressed that the change was not an attempt to abandon urban gospel but rather an effort to explore his creativity. “It wasn’t intentional. It was just me expressing myself, like testing my limits. I still do urban gospel. My latest song has more of an urban Afro vibe. But I felt like I had to push myself, push my limits,” he said. Perez Musik argued that artistes should be free to experiment with different musical styles as long as the message they communicate remains clear. “I love to explore different sounds and I don’t see anything wrong with that. I have a problem with it when people categorise and segment. I think it’s just music,” he said. He said musicians should be able to move between ballads, R&B, soul, alternative music and other styles without being restricted by the genre with which audiences first identify them. For Perez Musik, the problem is partly rooted in how Ghanaian audiences associate people with the first thing for which they become known. “Ghanaians have a way of boxing you. That’s why we call every toothpaste, we call every bath soap Key Soap,” he said. He said some people in the contemporary music space still do not regard him as a contemporary artiste because of his association with urban gospel. Despite the challenges, Perez Musik said he remains grateful for the progress he has made. “But I think it’s just the grace of God that has brought me this far. It’s just the grace and the mercy of God. And I don’t take that for granted at all,” he said.

items.title: My faith shapes my comedy — Mr Aloy
items.description: Nigerian actor and content entrepreneur, Emmanuel Chinedum Okonkwo, popularly known as Mr Aloy, has said his Christian faith plays a major role in shaping his comedy and determining the kind of content he produces. Mr Aloy, who is known for family-oriented comedy, social commentary and moral-themed content, said his Christian convictions influence the subjects he chooses to explore and those he deliberately avoids. According to the entertainer, although comedy is primarily meant to entertain, he believes it should also promote positive values and contribute meaningfully to society. He said he does not deliberately mock sacred Christian expressions in his comedy, stressing that his faith remains an important part of his identity as he pursues a career in the entertainment industry. For Mr Aloy, the principle also extends beyond comedy, as he believes wealth and success should be pursued in ways that positively impact society and ultimately serve God. His philosophy comes against the backdrop of his transition from a medical laboratory technician to a digital entertainer. The artiste studied Medical Laboratory Technology at the Anambra State College of Health Technology before relocating to Lagos in 2008, a move that eventually changed the course of his career. Rather than using money initially intended for a trip to Europe, he invested it in importing laboratory equipment. The decision led to the establishment of Memshack Medics, a business that later expanded into the medical equipment sector. However, entertainment remained a strong passion for him. His interest in acting was nurtured through church drama, where he became actively involved in the drama department and eventually headed the unit. The experience encouraged him to pursue Nollywood, prompting him to attend auditions in Lagos, particularly in Surulere. Mr Aloy has recounted spending years working around the Nigerian film industry before he began receiving significant financial rewards. At some point, he also paid to attend auditions while struggling to establish himself. His first Nollywood appearance was in Destruction Instinct, where he played a corrupt police officer. With the rapid growth of social media entertainment and skit-making in Nigeria, Mr Aloy gradually moved from conventional acting into digital comedy. His early content explored provocative themes, but after his Facebook page encountered monetisation challenges, he reassessed his approach. He subsequently focused more on family-oriented comedy, social issues, moral lessons and messages encouraging people to appreciate their parents and value relationships. He has also worked with established Nollywood figures, including Bolanle Ninalowo, Funke Akindele and Nkem Owoh, whom he has identified as one of his inspirations. Despite his energetic comic persona, Mr Aloy describes himself as a serious-minded individual who remains focused on his family, business and career. items.title: Cross River Gov Otu halts unauthorised clan, village creation exercise
items.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, Calabar CALABAR — Cross River State Governor, Senator Bassey Otu, has ordered the immediate suspension of an ongoing Clan and Village Creation exercise in the state, declaring that the process was neither authorised nor approved by his administration. The directive was conveyed in a statement by the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Ededem Ani, who said the Governor’s attention had been drawn to the exercise being conducted by the office of the Special Adviser to the Governor on Chieftaincy Affairs. Ani said the exercise “was neither authorised nor approved by his office,” stressing that it “does not carry the imprimatur of the State Government, and cannot be allowed to continue or to be given any further effect.” The Attorney-General said the government’s decision was also informed by a pending legal action before the High Court of Cross River State, Calabar. He quoted the Governor as directing that all activities connected with the exercise, including the processing, verification or publication of any Clan or Village Creation List, be terminated immediately. The statement read: “No further steps be taken by your office or any officer under your supervision towards the creation, recognition or conferment of Clan or Village status on any community pending further directive from the government.” The directive further reiterated that the Governor’s approval remained a mandatory prerequisite for any clan or village creation exercise in the state. It warned that “no Clan or Village Creation exercise may be embarked upon by your office, or any officer under its supervision, without the prior approval of His Excellency the Governor.” Ani consequently directed the Special Adviser on Chieftaincy Affairs to treat the Governor’s order with “the seriousness it deserves” and ensure “strict and immediate compliance.” The development underscores the administration’s position that processes relating to the recognition and administrative status of communities must be undertaken within the framework of lawful governmental authority. ECG announces power outages in parts of Greater Accra and Volta Region
items.description: The Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) has announced power outages affecting parts of the Greater Accra and Volta regions due to damaged electricity infrastructure and emergency maintenance works. In the Accra West Region, ECG said an outage affecting Sowutuom and surrounding communities was caused by broken high-tension poles at Sowutuom. The affected areas include Sowutuom Mambo, Glorious Jesus, Ablekuma Fanmilk, Ablekuma Abease, God First, Roman Park, Piteo Junction, Vicollis and Olebu Melcom, as well as adjoining communities. According to ECG, its engineers are working to repair the damaged infrastructure and restore electricity supply to the affected areas. The company did not provide a specific restoration time for the Sowutuom outage but said its technical teams were attending to the fault. ECG has also announced two separate emergency maintenance exercises in the Volta Region for Thursday, August 13. The first exercise is scheduled to take place between 9:00 am and 4:00 pm to enable engineers to work on a fault affecting electricity supply. Communities expected to experience the temporary outage include Sokode Ando, Sokode Gbagble, parts of Sokode Gborgame and surrounding areas. A second emergency maintenance exercise will take place on the same day from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm. The affected areas are Payin, Dzodze, Ziope, Akporkope, Agortime, Kpetoe and surrounding communities. ECG said the planned interruptions are necessary to allow its engineers to carry out work on faults affecting the electricity network. The company apologised for the inconvenience caused by the Sowutuom outage and the scheduled maintenance exercises, and said the work was being undertaken to address faults and restore reliable electricity supply.

items.title: Incumbent Western North NPP Regional Chairman withdraws from seeking re-election
items.description: The incumbent Western North Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Benjamin Armah, has withdrawn from the race to seek re-election ahead of the party’s regional executive elections. Mr Armah said the decision followed deep reflection and extensive consultations with his family, friends, and key stakeholders, as well as his desire to serve the broader interests of the NPP in the Western North Region. In a statement issued in Sefwi Wiawso, he said the decision was not taken lightly but was necessary to prioritise the unity, stability, and strategic strength of the party over personal ambition. “This is a moment for unity, not division; consolidation, not fragmentation; and collective purpose, not personal ambition,” he stated. Mr Armah expressed appreciation to party members across the region, particularly constituency executives, electoral area coordinators, polling station executives, delegates, grassroots activists, elders, and patrons who supported his candidature. He said after consultations with key stakeholders, he had decided to offer his “full and unequivocal support” to McDaniels Nyame. Mr Armah described Mr Nyame as a dedicated party member with proven loyalty to the NPP’s traditions and values, as well as organisational competence and political maturity. “Having had the opportunity to work closely with Mr McDaniels Nyame over the years, I have witnessed first-hand his dedication to the NPP. “I am persuaded that he possesses the temperament, experience, organisational capacity, and leadership qualities required to consolidate our gains, heal divisions where they exist, energise our grassroots, and provide the strategic direction necessary to reposition the Western North Region for the political tasks ahead,” he said. He consequently called on his supporters, delegates, and party executives who backed his candidature to transfer their confidence, energy, and support to Mr Nyame. Mr Armah stressed that his decision to withdraw from the contest did not mean he was stepping away from party activities. “My withdrawal from this contest does not represent a withdrawal from service to our Party. On the contrary, I remain fully committed to the New Patriotic Party and shall continue to serve, in whatever capacity necessary, with dedication, humility, loyalty, and integrity,” he said. He further called on NPP members in the region to remain united to strengthen the party’s chances of winning the 2028 general election. The Western North NPP is expected to hold its regional executive elections in the coming weeks as the party begins its reorganisation ahead of the 2028 general election.

items.title: Government targets local production of Zonda vehicle components under 24-hour economy
items.description: Government is pushing for the local production of selected components used in vehicles assembled by Zonda as part of efforts to deepen Ghana’s manufacturing capacity and create more jobs under the 24-hour economy. Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang said identifying vehicle parts that could be manufactured locally would create opportunities for Ghanaian businesses and expand employment across the manufacturing value chain. “I will be very happy going forward if we can even isolate one or two parts that we can produce locally,” she said. The Vice President made the remarks after observing operations at the Zonda vehicle assembly facility, where workers operate in shifts around the clock. She said the continuous operations demonstrate the potential of the government’s 24-hour economy to increase production and create more employment opportunities. Professor Opoku-Agyemang stressed the need for closer collaboration between government and local manufacturers to identify areas where Ghanaian companies can participate in the vehicle assembly value chain. She said producing selected components locally would help strengthen domestic businesses while building the technical skills of Ghanaian workers. It could also create opportunities for businesses in related industries that supply parts and services to the automotive sector. Government therefore intends to work with manufacturers and other stakeholders to identify components that can be produced locally and gradually increase Ghanaian participation in vehicle production. The initiative forms part of broader efforts to strengthen local industry, reduce reliance on imported components and retain more value within the Ghanaian economy. Government believes expanding local content in vehicle assembly could also support the wider objectives of the 24-hour economy, particularly through increased production, industrialisation and job creation.

items.title: Food security: Sanwo-Olu inaugurates Agege food hub, targets lower prices
items.description: …Mushin hub records over N4bn transactions in three years By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, on Wednesday inaugurated the Mid-Level Agro-Produce Hub at Pen Cinema, Agege, describing the facility as a key component of the state’s efforts to strengthen food security and reduce the cost of food for residents. Speaking at the inauguration, Sanwo-Olu said the hub was more than a market facility, describing it as part of the state’s broader strategy to transform the food system from production to distribution and consumption. “Today marks another important milestone in our collective journey to build a food-secure, economically vibrant, and resilient Lagos. “This facility represents our commitment to bringing modern food infrastructure closer to the people, to the communities where Lagosians buy, sell and consume food every day,” he said. The governor said Lagos’ food economy was valued at more than N16 trillion, while over 70 per cent of food consumed in the state was produced outside it. He identified high transportation costs, post-harvest losses, inadequate storage facilities and price volatility as some of the challenges affecting food distribution in the state. Sanwo-Olu said his administration launched the Lagos State Food Systems Transformation Agenda in 2021 to address the challenges. At the centre of the initiative, he said, was the Lagos Central Food Systems and Logistics Hub at Ketu-Ereyun, Epe, which is designed to become the largest food logistics hub in Sub-Saharan Africa when completed. According to him, the Epe hub is designed to handle more than 1.5 million metric tonnes of food annually and service over 1,500 food trucks daily. He said construction of the facility was at an advanced stage and would be commissioned before the end of his administration. The Agege facility is the third in the network of mid-level agro-produce hubs being developed by the state. The first, the Fresh Food Hub in Mushin, commissioned in December 2023, has recorded transactions worth more than N4 billion across 228 market days, with over 850 registered vendors and more than 7,000 direct and indirect jobs created. The second hub, located in Abijo, was commissioned earlier this year by President Bola Tinubu. “These hubs shorten supply chains, reduce unnecessary layers of intermediation, improve produce handling and make food distribution more efficient,” Sanwo-Olu said. The governor also highlighted the Produce for Lagos Programme, launched in July 2025 alongside a N500 billion Offtake Guarantee Fund. He said the programme was designed to shift agriculture from a supply-driven to a demand-driven model by guaranteeing farmers access to markets in Lagos, thereby addressing challenges relating to financing and market access. Sanwo-Olu disclosed that construction was ongoing at Opebi and Bombata, while additional hubs were planned for Ikorodu, Apapa, Festac and the Lekki axis. He said the long-term objective was to establish structured food hubs across all Local Government Areas and Local Council Development Areas in the state. Beyond infrastructure, the governor said more than 125,800 farmers and fishermen had been trained under his administration. He added that over 4,000 youths had been trained through the Lagos Agripreneurship Programme, while the Lagos Agric Scholars Programme was operating in more than 440 secondary schools. The Lagos Butchers Academy, he said, was also training meat processors in modern and hygienic practices. Sanwo-Olu cited the Lagos Rice Mill at Imota, described as Africa’s largest, saying it produced more than 250,000 50kg bags of Eko Rice in the past year, including the newly introduced Eko Fortified Rice aimed at addressing malnutrition. “May this hub bring prosperity to the traders who will work here, better prices to the farmers who will supply it, and fresh, affordable food to every family it serves,” he said. Facility to accommodate 400 vendors Commissioner for Agriculture and Food Systems, Abisola Olusanya, said the Agege hub was conceived as part of an interconnected food distribution network, with the Epe facility serving as the central hub and the mid-level hubs distributing food closer to communities. She said the Agege project was developed in partnership with Origin Tech Group, the project ideator and developer. According to Olusanya, the network was designed to address food losses resulting from poor handling and inadequate storage, congestion caused by food trading and transportation, and the poor conditions under which some traders operate. She said the Agege facility occupies approximately 7,000 square metres and has a 4,000-square-metre trading floor capable of accommodating between 350 and 400 vendors. The facility also has about 1,200 square metres of dry storage with a capacity of 800 tonnes and approximately 300 tonnes of cold storage. Olusanya disclosed that full operations would commence in six weeks to allow for the onboarding of operators and completion of the necessary operating, logistics and governance systems. She said a 351-page operating framework had also been developed to guide activities at the hub, including produce reception, quality control, storage, inventory management, sanitation, waste management and trading operations. The Executive Chairman of Agege Local Government Area, Vinod Obasa, described the commissioning as a new chapter in the economic development of the area. Obasa said the project aligned with the local government’s commitment to development and economic empowerment. He urged residents, traders, farmers, entrepreneurs and investors to embrace and protect the facility, stressing that while government could provide infrastructure, its success depended on the people. The Agege Mid-Level Agro-Produce Hub is expected to serve Agege and neighbouring communities while strengthening the wider food distribution network across Lagos. The post Food security: Sanwo-Olu inaugurates Agege food hub, targets lower prices appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Londres voudrait renouer le dialogue militaire avec Moscou
items.description: Le Royaume-Uni souhaiterait retablir les contacts directs avec le commandement militaire russe afin de reduire le risque qu'un incident ne provoque une confrontation entre les deux pays, rapporte le 11 août le Times , qui cite plusieurs sources. Les echanges au plus haut niveau militaire seraient interrompus depuis pres de quatre ans. Le Times affirme que le dernier entretien entre Valery Guerassimov, chef d'etat-major general des forces armees russes, et son homologue britannique remonterait a septembre 2022, lorsque ce poste etait occupe par l'amiral Tony Radakin. Cette chronologie est toutefois contredite par les informations communiquees a l'epoque par le ministere russe de la Defense, puis relayees par Reuters. Un echange entre les deux responsables a bien eu lieu apres cette date. Le 24 octobre 2022, Valery Guerassimov s'etait notamment entretenu par telephone avec Tony Radakin. Selon le ministere russe de la Defense, les deux responsables avaient notamment poursuivi leurs discussions sur la situation liee a une eventuelle utilisation par l'Ukraine d'une « bombe sale ». Ce n'est donc qu'apres cette conversation que les contacts semblent s'etre interrompus. D'apres le Times , de nouvelles tentatives de Tony Radakin pour joindre le general russe seraient ensuite restees sans resultat, Moscou ayant fait savoir que Valery Guerassimov etait trop occupe pour lui repondre. Son successeur, le marechal en chef de l'Air Richard Knighton, nomme en septembre dernier, aurait lui aussi « tente » d'etablir un contact avec le chef d'etat-major russe, sans obtenir de reponse. La question revient desormais au premier plan a Londres. Toujours selon le quotidien, le nouveau ministre britannique de la Defense, Wes Streeting, est appele a retablir les canaux de communication avec l'armee russe. Plusieurs hauts responsables et diplomates britanniques s'inquietent en particulier du risque d'une escalade involontaire. Un incident dans les eaux proches du Royaume-Uni pourrait, selon eux, entraîner les deux pays dans une confrontation beaucoup plus large. John Foreman, ancien attache militaire britannique a Moscou et a Kiev, a estime que la « gravite de la situation internationale pourrait justifier de nouvelles methodes pour maintenir le dialogue ». Un autre ancien haut grade britannique a de son cote juge qu'aucune desescalade durable n'etait possible en l'absence de communication. Incident dans la Manche Le 16 juin dernier, un incident s'est produit dans la Manche entre la fregate russe Amiral Grigorovitch et un yacht britannique. Selon le ministere russe de la Defense, le yacht britannique suivait une trajectoire susceptible de provoquer une collision avec le bâtiment militaire. Apres plusieurs tentatives de prise de contact par radio restees sans reponse, puis l'envoi de signaux sonores et de fusees de signalisation, l'equipage russe a finalement tire des coups de semonce avec des armes legeres alors que les deux navires n'etaient plus separes que d'environ 150 metres. Le yacht britannique a alors modifie sa route et s'est eloigne. Aucun blesse ni degât n'a ete signale. Le ministere russe de la Defense a souligne que l'equipage de la fregate Amiral Grigorovitch avait agi en stricte conformite avec les regles internationales de navigation et pris toutes les mesures necessaires pour eviter l'incident. Les relations entre Londres et Moscou etaient deja au plus bas avant le debut de l'operation militaire speciale russe en Ukraine. En fevrier 2022, quelques jours avant son lancement, Sergueï Choïgou, alors ministre russe de la Defense, avait rencontre son homologue britannique Ben Wallace. Il avait decrit la cooperation entre les deux pays comme « pratiquement inexistante », tout en soulignant que Moscou ne souhaitait pas voir la situation se deteriorer davantage.

items.title: NEITI report: EFCC recovers N115bn for NDDC, clears 19 oil firms
items.description: … Senate intensifies probe of 2021–2023 oil and gas audit By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has recovered more than N115 billion in outstanding statutory levies owed the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) by some oil companies between 2021 and 2023. The commission disclosed this on Wednesday before the Senate Committee on Public Accounts, which is investigating findings contained in the 2021–2023 Oil and Gas Sector Audit Report of the Nigeria Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (NEITI). The EFCC representative, Francis Oka-Phillips Usani, told the committee, chaired by Senator Ibrahim Dankwambo (PDP, Gombe North), that the recovered liabilities comprised N76.883 billion and $81.076 million. Usani said the commission investigated 43 oil companies, adding that 24 companies operating within the Niger Delta were found to have outstanding liabilities relating to the three per cent statutory levy payable to the NDDC. He said the remaining 19 companies were cleared after the investigation. “At the commencement of investigation, EFCC invited 43 oil companies, out of which 24 operating within the Niger Delta were found to have outstanding liabilities in the sums of N76,883,705,907.17 and $81,076,655, while the remaining 19 other oil companies were given clean bill of health,” he said. According to him, following the investigation and pressure mounted on the affected companies, some of them paid their outstanding liabilities directly to the NDDC. He said the payments amounted to N6.709 billion and $16.994 million. Usani further disclosed that of the funds recovered by the commission on behalf of the NDDC, N73.373 billion and $67.070 million had been released to the commission, while N3.510 billion and $14.005 million remained in the EFCC recovery account. On the scope of the investigation, Usani said the EFCC focused primarily on unpaid three per cent statutory levies due to the NDDC as identified in the NEITI report. He, however, said the commission was mindful that there could be other unpaid statutory obligations and taxes due to the Federal Government. Senate summons oil company chiefs Following the EFCC’s presentation, the committee rejected an attempt by TotalEnergies EP Nigeria Limited to respond to queries raised against the company in the audit report, citing inadequate representation. The committee consequently directed the Managing Director of TotalEnergies to appear in person at a date to be fixed next week. It also gave the managing directors of South Atlantic Petroleum Limited, Oando Oil Limited, Famfa Oil and Green Energy International Limited a final opportunity to appear physically before the committee. At the end of the session, Dankwambo said the investigative hearing would continue on Thursday. a critical part of the mobile money ecosystem. ‎Speaking at the engagement, Samuel Sarpong, Sales and Distribution Director at Telecel Ghana, said agents play an important role in the growth of the company’s telecom and mobile money business.‎ ‎According to him, the training is intended to equip agents with the knowledge and skills required to provide better services to customers.‎ ‎“We are working with the MoMAG of Ghana as a mobile money agent network to collaborate on our various efforts to improve their capability as agents.”‎ ‎He added that the agent network is an important part of the telecom and cash business ecosystem, making continuous capacity building necessary.‎ ‎“One of the best ways is to equip them through this kind of capacity training so that they’ll be better positioned to serve our customers better.”‎ ‎The President of the Mobile Money Advocacy Group Ghana, Edward Ofori Agyemang, said the partnership with Telecel is part of a broader effort to collaborate with electronic money issuers to address challenges confronting mobile money agents.‎ ‎He cited fraud and attacks by armed robbers as some of the major threats facing agents across the country.‎ ‎“We all know in the country how fraud is going on, how armed robbers are killing our agents.”‎ ‎Mr Ofori Agyemang stressed the need for agents to receive continuous training to enable them to operate professionally and protect their businesses.‎ ‎He also highlighted customer relations as an important area requiring attention, particularly for agents who may lack the skills to communicate effectively with customers.‎ ‎“Some of the agents who don’t know how to talk to customers, how to relate to customers, and customers are the people who give us the money.”‎ ‎According to him, the collaboration with Telecel is therefore aimed at ensuring that agents understand how to run their businesses professionally and in accordance with applicable regulations.‎ ‎“We have partnered with Telecel Ghana to train our agents to make sure that the businesses they are doing, they would make sure that they do everything in compliance with regulations.”‎ ‎Top-performing agent welcomes initiative ‎For some agents, the training has provided an opportunity to gain new knowledge and better understand Telecel’s mobile money operations.‎ ‎James Ablo, a top-performing Telecel agent, described the programme as beneficial and said the lessons would help him improve his business.‎ ‎“Today’s program is very helpful to me. I’ve learned a lot.”‎ ‎Mr Ablo disclosed that he had previously encountered some challenges with Telecel but said the engagement had given him a new perspective and useful information.‎ ‎“I’m someone who has issues with Telecel, but now that I’ve been here today, it’s my first time.”‎ ‎He said the knowledge gained from the programme would help boost his business, particularly in relation to Telecel’s mobile money services.‎ ‎“I’ve learned something that is going to boost my business, especially in terms of Telecel mobile money issue.”‎ ‎Mr Ablo also expressed his intention to share what he had learnt with people within his community and educate them about the benefits of Telecel’s services. ‎“As I’m going, I hope I’m going to teach people around my area what the benefits in Telecel and so far what Telecel is doing for the country.”‎ ‎The collaboration comes as mobile money agents continue to serve as an important point of access to digital financial services for customers across Ghana.‎ ‎The organisers believe that equipping agents with knowledge in customer service, fraud awareness, regulatory compliance and business management will help strengthen trust within the mobile money ecosystem.‎ ‎The initiative also seeks to ensure that agents can operate more professionally while building sustainable and profitable businesses. ‎For Telecel and MoMAG, the focus is ultimately on developing an agent network that is safe, trusted, professional and better equipped to serve customers.

items.title: 'We aspire for it to grow': Turkiye's Erdogan eyes expansion of Makkah Joint Defence Agreement
items.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said on Wednesday that he hoped more countries would join a defence agreement signed last week between Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, aimed at stabilising a region wracked by conflict. The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed on Friday as the Middle East grapples with fallout from the US-Iran war , which has dragged in regional players and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. “Our vision for it is not limited to the three countries,” the Turkish leader told the London-based Asharq Al-Awsat daily. “Rather we aspire for it to grow, and perhaps appropriate conditions will emerge one day for all countries of the region to gather under its umbrella.” Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on Saturday said Turkiye expected Egypt to join the pact “in the next stage”, telling the Anadolu state news agency only “a few technical issues” stood in the way. Egypt has not commented on the agreement nor on the remarks by Fidan, who will visit Cairo on Thursday and Friday. Cairo has robust military cooperation with Ankara, but has given no indication it intends to sign up to the new security alliance, which contains a Nato-style clause saying any attack on one would be seen as an attack on all. The five-month US-Iran war has upended the security architecture in the region and forced a rethink of decades of conventional wisdom rooted in US military supremacy. Erdogan said the pact emerged out of the “new circumstances” in the Middle East with regional players seeking to assume greater responsibility for their own security and stability. “Regional issues should be resolved by regional actors, and with this action, we consider that we have taken a first step toward achieving that goal,” he told the Saudi-owned newspaper. “Resolving regional issues must be carried out away from formulas imposed from the outside. We know very well that solutions imported from abroad only bring disasters.” The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement has been hailed by the 57-member Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) as an “important strategic step”. Kuwait , Bahrain and Somalia are among the countries that have welcomed it. Iran’s comments also took a rather positive tone, stressing its stance of pursuing “security mechanisms based on cooperation between regional countries”. On Monday, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif affirmed that the defence pact was “entirely for defensive purposes ”, and not for any aggression. Addressing the federal cabinet on Monday, PM Shehbaz stressed that the objective of the pact is to “promote peace, progress, and prosperity in the region”. While the pact comes in the backdrop of the US-Israel war on Iran, Bloomberg had reported in January — before the conflict began — that Ankara was seeking to join a separate mutual defence pact between Islamabad and Riyadh. Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already signed the “ Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement ” in Riyadh last September, pledging that any attack on either nation would be treated as an act of aggression against both. In January, Reuters quoted Defence Production Minister Raza Hayat Harraj as saying that a draft had been prepared after 10 months of talks. Turkish FM Hakan Fidan had said Ankara favoured an “inclusive platform that creates wider, bigger cooperation and stability”. Pakistan has also sought to mediate efforts to end the US-Iran war, while Turkiye has played a diplomatic role in negotiations aimed at ending the war in Gaza. Israel ‘removing Palestine’ from world agenda Erdogan also accused the Israeli government of Benjamin Netanyahu of seeking to “remove Palestine” from the world’s agenda. “The aim of the Netanyahu government is to remove Palestine from the common agenda of humanity by profiting from chaos and new conflicts in the region,” Erdogan said at a joint news conference with his Palestinian counterpart, Mahmoud Abbas. “No matter what they do, they will not succeed. The Palestinian cause will continue to grow in people’s hearts as they try to destroy it,” he stressed, vowing Turkiye would fight for the establishment of a Palestinian state. A strong advocate of the Palestinian cause, Erdogan has repeatedly lambasted Netanyahu’s government, accusing the Israeli prime minister of committing “genocide” in Gaza and of pursuing expansionist policies in the West Bank, Lebanon, Syria and beyond. Abbas arrived in Ankara on Tuesday accompanied by his diplomatic adviser Majdi Khalidi, intelligence chief Majed Faraj and senior Palestinian official Ziad Abu Amr. He met Erdogan on Wednesday with the pair discussing developments in the region in talks the Palestinian leader described as “important and fruitful”. “I hope the decision to hold legislative and presidential elections in Palestine after a long time will bring good fortune … [and] will advance the reconciliation process,” Erdogan said, in a nod to the historic rivalry between Abbas’ Fatah movement and Gaza’s Hamas rulers. Abbas also hailed the defence pact between Ankara, Riyadh and Islamabad, saying it was “of utmost importance” and expressing hope it would help enhance security and stability in the region.

items.title: La Russie propose plusieurs échanges de prisonniers, mais Kiev refuse de reprendre les siens
items.description: « La Russie mene un travail systematique et coherent dans le cadre du processus d'echange, en cooperation avec le ministere russe de la Defense et les services competents. Nous transmettons regulierement a la partie ukrainienne les listes de nos citoyens qui sont attendus chez eux. Cependant, malheureusement, Kiev refuse souvent les propositions que nous soumettons, ils ne veulent pas recuperer tous leurs militaires et, surtout, ils ne sont pas presses de rendre les notres », a declare, ce 12 août, la commissaire russe aux droits de l'homme, Iana Lantratova, denoncant l'indifference de Kiev au sort des prisonniers. Iana Lantratova a indique que trois listes differentes avaient ete proposees a l'Ukraine au cours du seul mois ecoule. Elles comprenaient aussi bien des militaires ukrainiens que des personnes condamnees en Russie pour differentes infractions. D'apres elle, aucune de ces propositions n'a permis d'aboutir, la partie ukrainienne refusant de reprendre certains de ses propres ressortissants. La Russie a notamment etabli une liste de 224 Ukrainiens condamnes pour des crimes commis sur le territoire russe. La commissaire assure que Moscou est pret a les remettre rapidement en echange de citoyens russes detenus par l'Ukraine, notamment des personnes originaires de la Republique populaire de Donetsk, de la Republique populaire de Lougansk et de Crimee qui se trouvent en captivite depuis 2014 ou 2022. Elle reproche a Kiev de ne pas accepter cette formule et estime que les autorites ukrainiennes privilegient la communication politique au sort des personnes concernees. Lantratova a egalement reagi a la publication par la partie ukrainienne des listes de prisonniers originaires de ces territoires que Moscou refuserait, selon Kiev, d'inclure dans les echanges. Elle conteste cette presentation et assure au contraire que ces noms figurent sur les listes etablies par la Russie en vue de leur rapatriement. Selon la commissaire aux droits de l'homme, Moscou attend desormais que Kiev donne son feu vert a l'echange propose. Iana Lantratova reproche aux autorites ukrainiennes de maintenir publiquement l'idee que certains prisonniers auraient ete « delaisses » par la Russie , alors que, selon elle, c'est precisement l'absence de reponse ukrainienne qui empeche leur retour. Elle affirme par ailleurs que Moscou ne fait aucune distinction entre les prisonniers russes en fonction de leur region d'origine, assurant que les autorites russes sont pretes a accepter des solutions difficiles et diverses afin d'obtenir le retour de chacun d'entre eux. S'adressant aux familles qui attendaient leurs proches, Lantratova a fait savoir que leurs demandes etaient entendues et que Moscou avait deja donne son accord a l'echange. Elle a insiste sur le fait qu'aucun prisonnier n'avait ete abandonne et que les demarches se poursuivaient pour obtenir leur retour.

items.title: 2026 Budget: Fubara denies rift with Rivers Assembly
items.description: By Daniel Abia, P/Harcourt The Rivers State Government has dismissed reports of a fresh disagreement between Governor Siminalayi Fubara and members of the State House of Assembly over the delay in the passage of the 2026 Appropriation Bill. The government described the reports as false and misleading, saying the budget proposal was undergoing the normal legislative process. In a statement issued on Wednesday by the Chief Press Secretary to the governor, Onwuka Nzeshi, the government said Fubara was working closely with the lawmakers in the interest of the state. “We wish to make it abundantly clear that His Excellency, Governor Siminalayi Fubara, is not at loggerheads with members of the Rivers State House of Assembly, but rather working closely with them to serve the good people of Rivers State,” Nzeshi said. He explained that the 2026 budget proposal had already been presented to the House of Assembly and was currently undergoing legislative consideration. “The 2026 budget proposal has been presented to the House of Assembly; it is going through the normal legislative process and we strongly believe that once the process is completed, it will be passed by the lawmakers,” he said. Nzeshi said the state government had gone through difficult times in the past and was not prepared to be drawn into another round of controversies. “We therefore advise all those bent on promoting negative narratives to desist from such actions forthwith, as we need peace and harmony to ensure steady development of Rivers State,” he added. The clarification comes against the backdrop of the political developments in the state and renewed attention on the relationship between the executive and legislative arms. Fubara’s decision to return to the political camp associated with the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, had earlier raised expectations that the budget would receive a smooth passage in the State House of Assembly. items.description: Speaker of Parliament Alban Sumana Kingsford Bagbin has recalled Parliament from recess for a five-day sitting to consider urgent parliamentary business. The recall will begin on Monday, August 24, and continue until Friday, August 28, at Parliament House in Accra. The directive was issued by the Speaker on Wednesday, August 12, in accordance with Order 58(4) of the Standing Orders of the Parliament of Ghana. In the directive, Speaker Bagbin exercised the power granted to him under the Standing Orders to recall Parliament notwithstanding the recess. The notice states that Parliament will sit from 12 noon on Monday, August 24, with proceedings continuing through Friday, August 28. The Speaker said the recall had been necessitated by the need for Parliament to consider urgent parliamentary business, although the notice did not specify the particular matters to be dealt with during the sitting.

items.title: Reps committee fails to sit over alleged fake agency probe
items.description: By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The House of Representatives Ad Hoc Committee investigating the controversial Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council (PFIPC) failed to sit on Wednesday as scheduled, raising fresh questions over the next phase of the probe. The committee had adjourned its previous investigative hearing to August 12 for the continuation of proceedings, with relevant government agencies and stakeholders expected to appear. However, the scheduled sitting did not hold, leaving journalists and other stakeholders without an official explanation. As of the time of filing this report, neither the committee nor its Chairman, Rep. Yusuf Gagdi, had issued a statement on why the hearing was not held or whether a new date had been fixed. The development came as the investigation approaches what the committee had earlier indicated could be the concluding stage of its public hearings, before members compile their findings and recommendations. How the controversy started The controversy centres on the PFIPC, an organisation that allegedly operated as a Federal Government agency despite claims that it was not established by law, executive order or any other valid government instrument. Questions arose after the purported council was included in the 2026 Appropriation Act, with about N1.3 billion allocated to it. The House subsequently constituted a 12-member ad hoc committee, chaired by Gagdi, to investigate how the organisation found its way into the Federal Government’s budget and operated within government structures. The probe has expanded to allegations involving forged official documents, acquisition of office space, use of government vehicle number plates and attempts to obtain recognition from various Ministries, Departments and Agencies. Alleged forged documents A major development before the committee was the discovery of documents allegedly linked to several government institutions. The Accountant-General of the Federation, Shamseldeen Ogunjimi, told the committee that his office acted on a letter purportedly emanating from the State House in processing a budget code for the council. He later stated that the letter did not originate from the Presidency. “The letter that was received by the Treasury was respectfully addressed as coming from the State House. That letter was never issued by the State House,” Ogunjimi said. The committee subsequently said it had uncovered about 29 allegedly forged official documents connected to the purported agency. The documents were reportedly traced to institutions including the State House, the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation and the Federal Ministry of Finance. The Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, Didi Esther Walson-Jack, also told the panel that due diligence was not sufficiently conducted in the handling of documents relating to the purported agency. Gagdi subsequently described the purported appointment letter of the alleged Director-General of the PFIPC, Adeniyi Adeyemi, as fake. Adeyemi’s appearance remains unresolved Another major issue in the investigation is the committee’s inability to publicly question Adeyemi, who presented himself as the Director-General of the purported council. The committee had earlier directed the Inspector-General of Police to produce Adeyemi within 48 hours, saying his testimony was necessary to resolve outstanding questions surrounding the organisation and the documents attributed to it. The police, however, informed the committee that Adeyemi was being held pursuant to a court order and could not be released to appear before the lawmakers without appropriate judicial authorisation. The committee subsequently resolved to question him at an undisclosed time and location to avoid interfering with ongoing criminal investigations by security and anti-corruption agencies. Adeyemi’s legal team, however, has argued that he should be allowed to respond to the allegations publicly, noting that other persons involved in the matter had appeared before the committee. Presidency disowns council The State House has also denied authorising the creation of the PFIPC or requesting a budget code for it. Appearing before the committee, the Director of Administration in the State House, Abdulkadir Idris, said the Presidency neither created the council nor wrote to the Accountant-General seeking a budget code for it. “We did not send any correspondence or request to the Office of the Accountant-General in respect of this council. We don’t even know anything about this council. We only heard about it when it started appearing in the news,” he said. The State House also disowned a purported document allegedly signed by one “Akande Adewale” as Director of Administration and Support Services, saying there was no such official or department in the Presidency. ICPC submits interim findings The development came shortly after the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) submitted its interim findings on the matter. The commission said its investigation established that Adeyemi was not appointed by the Federal Government or any authorised government institution and that the PFIPC was not established by law, executive order or any valid government instrument. It also said the appointment letter and other documents allegedly used by Adeyemi were forged, adding that the purported council had appropriated the identity, office and operational structures of the former Presidential Economic Advisory Council. However, the ICPC said it found no evidence that Federal Government funds were actually released or disbursed to the purported agency. It identified weaknesses in verification processes within some government institutions and recommended the prosecution of Adeyemi, administrative sanctions against officials whose negligence facilitated the alleged scheme, as well as institutional reforms to strengthen verification and internal controls. Fresh questions over probe The committee’s failure to sit on its announced date is likely to generate further questions, particularly as several issues remain unresolved and the investigation appears to be nearing its conclusion. The probe is expected to establish not only how the purported council emerged but also how it allegedly gained access to government facilities, appeared in the national budget and interacted with public institutions without being detected earlier. The central issue, therefore, extends beyond the allegations against Adeyemi to the institutional processes that allegedly allowed the organisation to operate. With Wednesday’s sitting aborted, attention will now turn to when the committee will reconvene and how its eventual findings will relate to the interim conclusions already reached by the ICPC. The post Reps committee fails to sit over alleged fake agency probe appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: SAF accused of civilian killings as RSF drones strike three states
items.description: The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) were accused on Wednesday of killing at least five civilians and wounding more than 10 others in North Kordofan, while paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) drones struck targets across River Nile, Khartoum and North Kordofan states, highlighting the growing threat to civilians beyond Sudan’s active front lines. The Emergency Lawyers Group accused the SAF of having killed at least five civilians and wounded more than 10 others, including women and children, in areas northeast of Jabra El Sheikh in North Kordofan. The group said an armed army vehicle travelled from Jabra El Sheikh towards farming and grazing areas, targeting farmers , shepherds and other unarmed civilians in their homes, farms and grazing grounds. There were no reported battles or clashes in the area at the time, according to the group. Among those killed were Sheikh Awadallah Abdullah, his son and another civilian. The group said other civilians were killed at separate locations and that soldiers detained several civilians before returning to Jabra El Sheikh. Radio Dabanga could not immediately obtain comment from the Sudanese army. The Emergency Lawyers Group condemned the attack and warned that deliberately targeting civilians outside the context of hostilities constitutes a serious violation of international humanitarian law and could amount to war crimes. It called for an independent investigation, the release of detained civilians and accountability for those responsible. ‘RSF drones strike three states’ RSF drones attacked sites in River Nile, Khartoum and North Kordofan states at dawn on Wednesday, with residents reporting intensive drone activity and explosions. In River Nile State, sources told Radio Dabanga that drones targeted sites near Ed Damer and Atbara. No casualties were immediately reported. In Khartoum, witnesses reported explosions in Omdurman and Bahri as drones flew overhead. Field sources said SAF air defences engaged drones attempting to strike targets in Omdurman. Field sources said the drones approached Omdurman from the southeastern part of Khartoum State. In El Obeid, North Kordofan, an RSF drone attack killed a woman and a man and wounded several others, local sources said. SAF air defences from the Fifth Infantry Division responded to the attack, while the wounded were taken to hospitals. The SAF had not immediately commented on the reported drone attacks. items.title: ‘How does Deputy AG know registrar hasn’t received Atta Akyea’s vacation absence letter?’ – Tuah-Yeboah asks
items.description: Former Deputy Attorney General has questioned the basis of the Deputy Attorney General’s claim that Samuel Atta Akyea, lead counsel for former National Signals Bureau Director Kwabena Adu-Boahene and his wife, Angela Adjei Boateng, had not formally written to the court to explain his inability to appear during the legal vacation. Mr Alfred Tuah-Yeboah said that, as a matter of practice, a lawyer who is unable to attend court formally communicates that decision to the judge through the court’s registrar. His comments follow claims by Mr Atta Akyea that he had formally written to the judge explaining why he could not attend court during the legal vacation and requesting that proceedings be postponed until the end of the vacation. However, the Deputy Attorney General reportedly said no such letter had been written to the judge, arguing instead that the communication had been sent to the Office of the Attorney General, which considered the reason given by Mr Atta Akyea to be frivolous. Mr Tuah-Yeboah challenged that account, insisting that the appropriate channel for such communication is through the registrar of the court. “You write to the judge through his registrar. It doesn’t get to him directly. It gets to the registrar. So where is the Deputy Attorney getting information from? Has he spoken to a court registrar to find out whether indeed he has received such a letter?” he asked. According to him, the registrar is the appropriate person to confirm whether a lawyer’s correspondence has been received on behalf of a judge. “The registrar is who can say, yes, we’ve not received any letter,” he stated. Mr Tuah-Yeboah further described claims about the registrar not receiving the letter as “rich and very curious”, arguing that such matters should be clarified by officials of the Judicial Service rather than inferred by political or executive actors. He insisted that where there is uncertainty over whether a communication has been formally received by the court, the appropriate approach is to verify the matter directly with the court registrar. “It doesn’t work with the Judicial Service. So you can ask people from the Judicial Service. They should speak for themselves,” he added.

items.title: El Mourouj | Mandat de dépôt contre le père qui a jeté ses deux fillettes du 3e étage
items.description: ​Le juge d'instruction près le Tribunal de première instance de Ben Arous a émis, ce mercred 12 août 2026, un mandat de dépôt à l'encontre du père qui a jeté ses deux fillettes du troisième étage d'un immeuble situé à El Mourouj 1. ​La chute tragique a causé la mort sur le coup de la plus jeune, âgée d'à peine six mois, des suites de graves blessures, alors que sa sœur, âgée de trois ans, a été transportée en urgence absolue à l'hôpital pour y recevoir d'intenses soins médicaux. Son état de santé est jugé extrêmement critique en raison de multiples fractures aux membres et au crâne. On notera que pour l'heure, aucune information n'a été donnée sur les circonstance de ce drame, alors que le père qui s'est rendue à la police est placé en détention. Y. N. items.title: Sourou/Lutte contre le paludisme : La délégation spéciale de Tougan s’attaque aux gîtes larvaires
items.description: BURKINA-SOUROU-LUTTE- PALUDISME Sourou/Lutte contre le paludisme : La délégation spéciale de Tougan s'attaque aux gîtes larvaires Tougan, 12 août 2026 (AIB) -Le Président de la délégation spéciale (PDS) de Tougan, Ouigou Tiendrebeogo, accompagné du Médecin-chef de district (MCD), Jérôme Nikiema, ainsi que d'une délégation de la mairie, a supervisé, le samedi 8 août 2026, une opération de curage des caniveaux dans la ville de Tougan en vue de lutter le paludisme. Selon le MCD, Jérôme Nikiema, cette activité s'inscrit dans le cadre d'une initiative du ministère de la Santé visant à renforcer la lutte contre le paludisme. « Le ministère de la Santé met en œuvre, à compter du mois d'août 2026, les Journées nationales de lutte antivectorielle, une initiative de lutte contre le paludisme à travers l'élimination des gîtes larvaires et l'assainissement de l'environnement », a-t-il expliqué. Le PDS, Ouigou Tiendrebeogo, a salué cette initiative du ministère, soulignant que « la santé est l'affaire de tous » et qu'elle commence par la propreté de notre cadre de vie. Il a invité les populations à préserver quotidiennement la salubrité de leur environnement en adoptant des comportements civiques. items.title: Nobody Knows What Ultra-Processed Food Is
items.description: You might know a tomato when you see one, but for the federal government, identifying one is harder. Is a tomato a fruit or a vegetable? In 1893, this question went all the way to the Supreme Court, which decided that, for tax purposes, at least, a tomato was a vegetable. What about milk? For a bureaucrat setting standards, a straightforward explanation such as “liquid from a cow’s udders” won’t quite cut it; according to the FDA, milk is “the lacteal secretion, practically free from colostrum, obtained by the complete milking of one or more healthy cows.” Even for the government, however, tomatoes and milk are relatively simple to define compared with ultra-processed foods. Although many researchers agree that these creations are negatively affecting people’s health, they cannot agree on what foods do and don’t belong in that category. That’s not keeping Robert F. Kennedy Jr. from trying: After months of promising the federal government’s first formal definition of ultra-processed foods, the secretary of Health and Human Services announced on Monday that the department is finalizing one. He stopped short, though, of sharing the exact text in either the public announcement or at a “food policy celebration” held Monday at HHS’s Washington headquarters; the definition is still being reviewed by the White House. This effort may have real upsides. Having a regulatory definition of ultra-processed foods (or UPF, as they’re often referred to) could at the very least advance inquiries into the harms of these products. But the effort also raises the question: Can the government adequately define a problem before researchers know its true cause? So far, scientific efforts to define UPF have revealed only how fuzzy the category is . The most commonly used definition, which was developed by Brazilian researchers, takes the most expansive approach: It lumps all foods with industrial ingredients, such as sweeteners and emulsifiers, into the ultra-processed category. A classification system created by academics at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, meanwhile, defines “highly processed foods” as products “processed to the extent that they are no longer recognizable as their original plant/animal source.” Yet another well-respected system, this one designed by a French analytics company, attempts to incorporate additional factors, such as a food’s salt, sugar, and fat content, as well as the “function, number, and potential health risk of additives.” These rubrics are distinct enough from one another that flavored yogurt is an ultra-processed food under the Brazilian system and a moderately processed food under the UNC system. Under the French system, the classification depends entirely on the yogurt itself (even though a paper from the group found that 95 percent of flavored yogurts in French grocery stores were indeed ultra-processed). Researchers disagree on how to define these foods, because the science around how and why they may be harmful is ambiguous. Epidemiological studies have found that UPF-heavy diets have consistently been associated with a range of maladies including cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes. But although researchers suspect that certain additives are causing dietary issues, the number of industrial ingredients or additives in Americans’ food is so large that many more may also be causing trouble. Nor do researchers know what processing steps cause everyday food ingredients to go from healthful to harmful. That means Kennedy and his department are essentially trying to define a food group that no one really understands. Kennedy is under no illusions about how little we know about the American food supply. He has frequently criticized a decades-old loophole that allows food companies to put new additives in their food without even telling the FDA. On Monday, he announced a new proposal to fix this issue; if finalized, the rule would require companies to let the FDA know when they’re introducing a new additive. But even that won’t fully solve America’s additive problem. Researchers at the Pew Health Group estimated in 2011 that America’s food supply already features more than 10,000 additives. The new rule would require manufacturers that quietly introduced such compounds to tell the FDA what those additives are but not to submit any scientific proof of the additives’ safety. And although the FDA can do its own review of such ingredients, that process is often glacially slow. (The agency still hasn’t completed its rereview of several chemicals nearly a year after announcing that it was taking a second look at their safety.) Plus, certain additives may be safe when consumed on their own but harmful when consumed alongside other additives. A study published last year found, for example, that consuming a cocktail of emulsifiers, a preservative, and a dye was associated with higher rates of type 2 diabetes but that several other industrial concoctions were not. If anything, researchers know less about how processing changes the ways humans digest certain foods. As the term ultra-processed implies, researchers believe that the ways food companies process individual ingredients has had a profound impact on our health. But because that concept is so new, very little research has been done on it. The Brazilian researchers, for example, have cited pre-frying as a mark of ultra-processing, even though it’s hard to imagine that precooking chicken nuggets could meaningfully affect how they’re digested. And although research does suggest that extrusion, which is used to make products such as cereal by pushing ingredients through a heated tube with rotating screws, makes it easier for the body to break down starches, the evidence of any ill effect on humans is limited. All of this makes Kennedy’s push to define UPF difficult. Any earnest effort to “Make America Healthy Again” cannot ignore the fact that a majority of the calories Americans consume come from ultra-processed foods, and that something in those foods seems to be making people ill. Creating a definition is an obvious first step toward addressing the issue, and the previous definitions for ultra-processed foods have undoubtedly advanced researchers’ understanding of those foods’ impact on our health. A 2019 study using the Brazilian definition found, for example, that people ate faster and gained more weight when fed an utlra-processed diet compared with an unprocessed one. But for researchers, the definition of UPF serves more as a hypothesis—an idea that they can test and adjust about how to think about this category of food. A government definition of UPF has a different purpose—it can prompt research, but it can also be used to make rules about how foods are tested, advertised, and sold. An overbroad definition could cost food companies millions in unnecessary costs and stoke unsubstantiated fear in consumers; a narrower definition, based on a hunch, could cause the same problems. Government definitions are not written in stone: In 2024, the FDA overhauled an outdated definition of healthy foods, which was issued amid the low-fat craze of the 1990s and excluded foods such as nuts and fatty fish. But the process of revising the definition took eight years. As Kennedy said Monday, “If you can’t define a problem, you can’t solve it.” But if you define a problem in the wrong way, you probably can’t solve it either.

items.title: Sanctions : le chocolat et la bière russes bannis en Lettonie pour des raisons de «moralité publique»
items.description: Les autorites lettones ont l'intention d'etendre les restrictions sur le commerce avec la Russie et la Bielorussie, en ajoutant a la liste des produits dont l'importation sur le territoire national est interdite les bonbons, les caramels, le chocolat, les biscuits et autres pâtisseries a base de farine, les sauces, les soupes toutes pretes, les boissons non alcoolisees et la biere provenant de ces deux pays, a rapporte le 11 août le site letton Press.lv. Selon les auteurs de l'article, le gouvernement a approuve les amendements proposes par le ministere de l'Agriculture, qui renforcent l'interdiction nationale d'importer ces produits en provenance de Russie et de Bielorussie. Press.lv precise que cette restriction s'appliquera quel que soit l'itineraire de livraison : les produits d'origine russe et bielorusse ne pourront pas etre importes sur le marche letton, meme via des pays tiers. En revanche, le transit par la Lettonie et les livraisons vers d'autres etats membres de l'UE ne sont pas concernes par ces restrictions, affirme l'article. Interdiction d'importer du chocolat et de la biere pour des raisons de « moralite publique » et de « securite » Le lendemain, le 12 août, le site Euractiv a rapporte , en citant une source, que la Commission europeenne avait soutenu l'instauration par la Lettonie de sanctions unilaterales sur les importations de produits russes. Un porte-parole de la Commission a souligne que, bien que la politique commerciale releve de la competence exclusive de l'UE, il existe des exceptions permettant a certains pays d'imposer de leur propre chef des restrictions, notamment des mesures fondees sur des considerations de « moralite publique, de politique publique ou de securite publique ». Selon Bruxelles, le gouvernement letton a justifie sa decision precisement par ces considerations. D'apres Euractiv, la Lettonie a pris cette mesure apres que la Commission europeenne n'a pas reussi a rassembler un soutien suffisant pour instaurer des restrictions sur le poisson russe au niveau de l'UE. Cette question s'est averee trop sensible pour les etats membres qui transforment d'importants volumes de poisson blanc, tels que la morue et le colin. De plus, la liste des personnes et des organisations deja visees par des sanctions est devenue si longue qu'il est de plus en plus difficile d'identifier de nouvelles cibles susceptibles de faire l'objet d'un consensus unanime. La Russie, pour sa part, considere les sanctions occidentales comme illegales. Le Kremlin a declare a plusieurs reprises que l'economie russe continuait de fonctionner malgre le grand nombre de sanctions imposees par les pays occidentaux. En juillet 2025, le porte-parole du president russe, Dmitri Peskov, a egalement souligne que la Russie avait developpe une certaine immunite face a ces restrictions.

items.title: Health Ministry clears salary arrears for 99% of 13,500 nurses, midwives
items.description: The Coalition of Unpaid Nurses and Midwives of Ghana has commended the Minister for Health, Hon. Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, for his intervention in resolving the salary arrears of nurses and midwives recruited in 2024. More than 99 per cent of the 13,500 affected health professionals have now received their salaries, following sustained engagement between the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Finance. President of the Coalition, Stephen Kwadwo Takyia, led a delegation to the Ministry of Health to formally express appreciation to the Minister and his officials for their efforts in addressing the group’s employment and salary concerns. Mr Akandoh explained that the affected health professionals had begun work without financial clearance, creating a difficult situation for Government. He said the Ministry, instead of withdrawing their appointments, chose to retain them at post while working with the Ministry of Finance to secure the necessary funding. According to the Minister, financial clearance has now been secured for all 13,500 workers, with only a few isolated cases yet to be resolved. He subsequently directed the Human Resource Directorate to expedite action on the outstanding cases. He also instructed health-sector agencies to fast-track the issuance of appointment letters and the mechanisation of newly recruited health professionals to ensure timely processing of their salaries. The Minister further disclosed that Government plans to recruit 16,000 health professionals in 2026, with financial clearance already secured for the first 8,000. He assured that clearance for the remaining 8,000 would be secured before recruitment begins to prevent a recurrence of salary arrears. Mr Akandoh urged newly recruited health professionals to report to their assigned facilities by August 20, 2026, warning that failure to report by the deadline could result in the loss of their appointments. He also encouraged health workers to serve with dedication and treat patients with respect and dignity, emphasising the need to keep patients at the centre of healthcare delivery. The Coalition expressed appreciation to the Minister and the Ministry for their continued engagement and support in resolving their concerns. Members expressed optimism that, with the payment challenges largely addressed, the group would soon no longer be known as the Coalition of “Unpaid” Nurses and Midwives.
